articles.title: Anthony Albanese apologises for hot-mic gaffe after Coalition criticises ‘locker-room talk’
articles.summary:
Prime minister says he and Chris Bowen were having ‘light-hearted banter’ when they were caught discussing where they keep their phones

Anthony Albanese has apologised for a hot-mic gaffe at…

blocks.text: Anthony Albanese has apologised for a hot-mic gaffe at the UN climate talks in Turkey, saying he regretted being overheard discussing mobile phone radiation and “dicks” in a candid conversation.
“I of course regret that. I apologise,” Albanese said during a visit to the Australian warship HMAS Stalwart in the Philippines on Sunday.
“This was a private conversation, we thought, between two friends having a bit of light-hearted banter.”

Ahead of a meeting at the Cop31 climate summit in Antalya on Friday, Albanese and the climate change minister, Chris Bowen, were caught on camera discussing which pocket they use to keep their mobile phone.

Albanese can be heard telling Bowen that he should store his phone away from his heart because “it can interfere with your rhythm”. Laughing, Bowen asks whether the advice was because a phone can be “a little bit radioactive”.
Albanese says “it makes absolute sense”, before Bowen replies that he was more conscious of putting his phone in his pants pocket. The prime minister asks: “Because of your dick?”
Bowen agrees and says: “Arguably more important than the heart.”
On Sunday, Albanese played down the incident which occurred ahead of a meeting with business leaders in Antalya.
“No one was hurt or harmed. We weren’t having private banter which criticised anyone,” he said.
The speedy apology is in contrast to previous gaffes by Albanese, including long-running controversy over comments about the gift of melons from Japan’s prime minister, Sanae Takaichi, on a podcast.
Albanese previously apologised for saying he would “shag” Australian singer Kylie Minogue in the same episode of the Bush Deep podcast.
after newsletter promotion
The melons comment risked becoming an international incident, as Albanese repeatedly insisted the comments and his corresponding hand gestures were not a reference to breasts.

Japan’s government sent a diplomatic cable to Australia in July, days after the podcast originally aired, claiming there had been “sensationalised reporting in the Australian media” and saying they detected no “ill intention” in Albanese’s statement.
The Coalition on Sunday criticised Albanese and Bowen’s comments.
Opposition frontbencher James Paterson said the remarks were unfortunate, telling News24 they could damage impressions of Australia on the world stage.
“That locker-room talk like that has a time and a place and it’s not at international summits when you’re the prime minister of Australia talking to your energy minister,” he said.
But the employment minister, Amanda Rishworth, dismissed the criticism, saying the comments were a joke.
“This is a private conversation in between meetings,” she said.
“I know that a hot-mic incident is very exciting for people ... but really, there are bigger issues to tackle and discuss.”
Earlier a spokesperson for the prime minister said the hot-mic comments were “a joke in between meetings”.
Albanese is in the Philippines for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit and high-level diplomatic meetings, including with the US president, Donald Trump.

articles.title: Marcos opens ASEAN plenary as South China Sea code likely to miss target
articles.summary: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. opened the plenary session of the 49th ASEAN Summit with a vow that all "priority economic deliverables" would be completed before Manila ends it chairship, but gave no…

blocks.text: November 15, 2026 | 11:41am

Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. arrives in a vehicle at the Philippine International Convention Center for the opening ceremonies of the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit and Related Meetings in Manila on November 15, 2026.
AFP / Rolex Dela Pena / Pool

MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. opened the plenary session of the 49th ASEAN Summit on Sunday, November 15, with a vow that all "priority economic deliverables" would be completed before Manila ends its chairship, but gave no timeline for the South China Sea code of conduct that it had hoped to conclude this year.

Speaking before other Southeast Asian leaders, Marcos said the Philippines had organized its chairship around "peace and security anchors, prosperity corridors, and people empowerment." Under security, he listed "advancing efforts on an effective and substantive code of conduct in the South China Sea in accordance with international law, including the 1982 UNCLOS."
"Advancing efforts" falls short of what Manila set out to deliver: that the long-stalled code of conduct would become one of its most significant diplomatic priorities as 2026 chair.

Dominic Xavier Imperial, the spokesperson of the Philippines' ASEAN chairship, said last week that negotiations for the code of conduct are now at "70%," without specifying the number of paragraphs that have been agreed upon.
But there have been no indications from the Philippine side that the original end-2026 deadline would be met, meaning talks will likely continue in 2027, when the chairship passes to Singapore.
It was the ASEAN foreign ministers themselves that set 2026 as the deadline for the code of conduct three years ago.
Imperial said last week that while there is a "commitment to finalize," Manila was keen on ensuring its "position on the elements that we want to be included in the COC are there."
"Our negotiators are doing the best they can to find a way to make more progress at the moment," Imperial had said at a November 13 briefing.
Progress on the code has long stalled due to unresolved issues on the agreement's geographic scope, the definitions of sensitive terms, and whether it should be legally binding.

That last point has stalled the talks for years as China has consistently resisted a legally binding code, which members such as the Philippines and Vietnam say is needed to hold Beijing accountable for its increasingly assertive actions in the South China Sea.
On the economy, Marcos said the 19 priority deliverables include the ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement, which was formally signed Saturday, November 14.
The signed agreement was formally presented at the opening ceremony earlier today.
Evolving economic challenges
Marcos, in his remarks, said the region's economies had to stay competitive "as technology, trade, energy requirements and supply chains evolve."
"The next task is to ensure that this network delivers greater benefits for our peoples," Marcos said, adding that partnerships should "turn political goodwill into practical cooperation."

"We should, therefore, continue to deepen our partnerships on the basis of mutual benefit, translate comprehensive and strategic partnerships and plans of action into concrete cooperation," the president added.
He also urged the leaders to "build on the ASEAN outlook on the Indo-Pacific as a basis for open, inclusive and practical engagement."

articles.title: PH, Australia sign defense cooperation agreement
articles.summary: The Philippines and Australia on Sunday formally signed an agreement that seeks stronger defense ties between the two countries.

blocks.text: Published November 15, 2026 11:26am
The Philippines and Australia on Sunday formally signed an agreement that seeks stronger defense ties between the two countries.
The defense cooperation agreement (DCA) was signed by Philippines Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. and Australian Ambassador to the Philippines H.E. Marc Innes-Brown.

Teodoro said the agreement will streamline the coordination between the Philippines and Australia when it comes to military and security matters, such as disaster response, military hardware procurement, and joint military exercises on land and at sea.

"Ngayon, ang bentahe talaga din nito sa disasters. At least, hindi na maraming permit-permit pa. Isahan na lang ito para agad maka-responde ang ating mga kaalyadong Australyano," said Teodoro in Filipino.
(Now, its real advantage in disasters is that, at least, there are no longer many permits required. It is streamlined into a single process so that our Australian allies can respond immediately.)
The agreement came after two countries signed an intent last year to formalize the deal in 2026.

Teodoro said the deal with Australia is different from the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement or EDCA between the US and the Philippines, which grants US troops access to designated Philippine military facilities and the right to construct facilities but rules out establishing a permanent base.

The Philippines, United States, Japan, and Australia will also establish a joint defense coordination center in Manila, the Combined Coordination Center (CCC), which aims to strengthen cooperation in domain awareness, information sharing, and military interoperability. —Vince Angelo Ferreras/RF, GMA News

articles.title: Judge temporarily blocks Trump from closing Washington DC golf course for renovation
articles.summary: It is the latest development in a months-long challenge to the president's plans for East Potomac Golf Links.

blocks.text: A federal judge has temporarily blocked the US government's closure of a historic golf course and park in Washington DC.
US District Judge Ana Reyes has been overseeing a months-long challenge to the president's plans for East Potomac Golf Links, which he said would be closed from 15 November for extensive renovations.
Reyes has said Donald Trump cannot close the park or its golf course, but added that his administration was not required to actively manage either.

Trump, an avid golfer, has said his plans to upgrade the 106-year-old course will create "one of the Best and Most Spectacular Golf Courses anywhere in the World". The BBC has contacted the White House for comment.

Declaring the current course "Trash Island", he announced in October it would be renovated over 15 months to create a space that "will be open to the Public while, at the same time, designed to the Highest Level of Golf and able to hold World Class Tournaments" - despite the ongoing litigation.

In a 30-page decision issued on Saturday, Reyes said the Trump administration's justifications for the proposed course closures were pretextual, and that the government violated at least two federal laws "to meet an arbitrary deadline."
"The Government proposes to close a historic park, daily enjoyed by Washingtonians of all stripes, indefinitely," Reyes wrote.

She said the closure "runs counter to the public interest in utilising national parkland", adding that the government had not "plausibly identified any harm it would suffer from a temporary restraining order that preserves the status quo pending further proceedings".
Her order will last until the 28 November.
The legal dispute dates back to February, when the DC Preservation League and others sued over redevelopment plans for the park.
The historic course, which sits 2 miles (3km) south of the White House, is one of three public courses run by the National Park Service in the nation's capital.
The legal fight then escalated in October, when the NPS began to cut down hundreds of trees without notifying Reyes until 15 hours before work was set to begin.
After the trees were cut, Reyes ordered the Trump administration to stop tree removal until at least 26 October and give her three business days' notice about making any other permanent changes.
Despite the work stoppage, Trump announced that the course would be closed for 15 months from 15 November to accommodate the renovations. He also shared a rendering of the course redesign.

"The current Course is old, broken, dilapidated, and of no further use or effect. It is in very poor condition, with falling, dangerous, and disease-infested trees and, importantly, a collapsing and hazardous seawall," he said in a post to Truth Social.
Reyes has since separately opened an inquiry into whether the justice department attorneys "have made misrepresentations to the court and otherwise violated ethical rules".

That included whether giving late notice to the court about the renovation plans was "done in bad faith" and whether the attorneys failed to correct previously false statements or withheld information.
She said she would carry out the inquiry with a special master, an independent third party.

articles.title: [Two Pronged] Worried my son is getting gym-obsessed because his dad came back
articles.summary: Is our letter sender worried her son is going to the gym too much? Or more concerned about her son's newly-kindled relationship with his absent dad?

blocks.text: Rappler’s People section runs an advice column by couple Jeremy Baer and clinical psychologist Dr. Margarita Holmes.

Jeremy has a master’s degree in law from Oxford University. A banker of 37 years who worked in three continents, he has been training with Dr. Holmes for the last 10 years as co-lecturer and, occasionally, as co-therapist, especially with clients whose financial concerns intrude into their daily lives.
Together, they have written two books: Love Triangles: Understanding the Macho-Mistress Mentality and Imported Love: Filipino-Foreign Liaisons.
Dear Dr Holmes and Mr Baer,

I am the mother of a 14-year old boy, “Percy,” my unico hijo and the reason I wake up in the morning. From the time he was born to now, he has been the biggest blessing in my life. I was a single mother and had no problem with that until his father Ahron came back into our lives (HIS life, really, but this affects me too). Anything that has to do with him, of course, has to do with me because he is my son and I have sole responsibility for him.

I was ok when Ahron first showed up because every boy needs a male role model and before his father, Percy never really had one. When Ahron started coming regularly, every Saturday afternoon (after lunch and before dinner which I notice I still had to take care of) to take his son out. But then, Ahron wanted to come every Wednesday afternoon too! I wanted to fight him in court but again, Percy was so happy to see him more often so I relented.

But I realized that Percy was changing. I found out that they always go to Ahron’s gym on Saturday, and now even every Wednesday!!! Ahron is a body builder, and has gotten my son “hooked.” Now Ahron’s friends are HIS friends too. But I also see that Percy, who used to be a loner, now has two friends who enjoy being with him when Ahron takes them all out to the gym.

True, these two friends are not the most popular boys in his class. Percy’s friends were not those I would have chosen for him, but at least now he has a barkada, (group of friends) which every boy needs.

Everybody says I am a worrywart, that I should be happy his father has now taken some responsibility for his son, and to focus on Percy’ happiness. But I am worried about their going to the gym too much. Isn’t there some sickness you can get if you do that too much? I do not want my husband infecting him with this.
– Rebecca
Dear Rebecca,
Thank you for your email.

You ask if too much gym can become a sickness and the answer is yes. Generally people go to the gym for health reasons or to become more fit (say, for sports) or to change their body shape in an effort to be more muscular, more “cut” (often, to be what they perceive is more attractive). Like most things in life, this is fine in moderation.

However, if gym work becomes an obsession, this can indicate body dysmorphia or muscle dysmorphia (also called bigorexia) which is basically a belief that one’s body is too small, skinny, or insufficiently muscular regardless of the objective reality. This is in effect reverse anorexia nervosa.

Your email does not suggest anything like this but does show that you have concerns about the influence Ahron has over Percy; you speak about Ahron “infecting him.” You do, however, recognize that there are positives in the relationship as well — he now has a father figure in his life and instead of being a loner now has a barkada and a new hobby.

Perhaps you simply need to adjust to the reappearance of Ahron in your lives. An ongoing dialogue with your husband about Percy’s progress will help you keep track of how Percy is handling the father/son dynamic.

Similar conversations with Percy will help you monitor his behavior. Keep an eye out nevertheless for red flags, such as any growing obsession with body size, supplement or steroid talk, significant diet changes, or injuries being brushed off.

You should however remember that despite these Saturday/Wednesday meetups, you remain the primary influence in Percy’s life: you provide him with a stable home and make the important decisions. Sharing him with your husband does not diminish your role or its value or negate the love you have for your son.
Best wishes,
-– JAF Baer

Thank you very much for your letter. While I believe, like Mr Baer, that bigorexia is not the major discomfort about Ahron coming back into Percy’s life, let me tell you the basics so you can either shelf the issue until it becomes a problem OR start researching on it even more and decide what other course of action you should take.
“Bigorexia” is a psychological condition and type of body dysmorphic disorder which, like anorexia, involves a distorted self-image.

People with anorexia, obsessed with losing weight, to the point of exercising obsessively and starving themselves. People with bigorexia are obsessed with becoming larger, more muscular and/or bulking up, to the point of obsessive exercise, supplement taking and even steroid use.

Your son seems a long way off from being vulnerable to bigorexia. What I see is a 14-year old boy, Percy, who knows for sure his mom loves him, but who is (as anyone would be his shoes) curious about his father and why he is no longer around.

Percy’s joy must have been so palpable you could not bear to curtail Ahron’s visits. Besides, I doubt you could deny what Percy and Ahron are entitled to, especially after all these years: time to get to know each other better, be together and build that unique relationship between father and son.

Ahron may have been a cad as your partner, but he is not necessarily going to be one with his son.So cut him some slack, Rebecca. In fact cut both of them some slack….especially since I feel your discomfort is not only because of Ahron’s sudden appearance.

Your disapproval could be triggered by the sense of unfairness of it all. Here you are, giving your all to this little one once he entered your life, secure in the knowledge that you and he were a team. And then, BAM! Just when he reached adolescence (a difficult enough time to begin with), who comes sauntering in but his father? Ahron, who got out when you need him most, and shows up now, when you have everything under control.

It is also not surprising that you would resent Percy for being so happy to see him each time Ahron picks him up. You can’t help feeling competitive and it is unfair of Percy to make you feel this way! Percy does not have the same history you had with Ahron, therefore, hard as it may be, withhold your disappointment of “Percy’s not seeing his father for who he is.” Forgive Percy for his joy at finally seeing, in flesh and blood, his father whom he has only imagined before this time.

Perhaps even more difficult, cut Arohn some slack too. Yes, he hurt you a lot, made you so angry, and betrayed your trust. But that is between the two of you, not between Ahron and Percy.The sooner Ahron and Percy can have their own relationship going with as little interference from you as possible (though recognizing sometimes this may be warranted) the better it will be not only for Ahron and Percy, but also for you. Of that I am certain.
All the best – MG Holmes
Life got complicated? Write to our Two Pronged duo at twopronged@rappler.com.

articles.title: Pope Leo speaks of community 'suffering' on visit to remote Andes town
articles.summary: Santa Cruz de Succhabamba is part of the Diocese of Chiclayo, where the pope served as bishop from 2015 to 2023.

blocks.text: On a visit to an isolated Andean village in his former diocese, Pope Leo XIV has spoken about the "suffering of those who are forced to leave their homeland in search of a better future", which he said had left communities under threat.

About 6,000 people live in Santa Cruz de Succhabamba, which is located in a remote part of the Andes mountains in northern Peru, but the Pope's visit drew a crowd of about 20,000, according to the Vatican.
At an outdoor Mass, Pope Leo spoke of "declining birth rates that are emptying villages," and the unequal distribution of the land's resources.
Over 40% of the population in the Cajamarca region, where the town is located, live in poverty - the highest figure in Peru, according to official data.
Cajamarca has lost the highest number of people to internal migration, with 729,000 people born there now living elsewhere in Peru.
In his sermon, Pope Leo thanked those who had made the journey to him and emphasised the importance of never losing heart, despite life's difficulties.

Santa Cruz is within the Diocese of Chiclayo, where Pope Leo served as bishop from 2015 to 2023. During his tenure, he visited Santa Cruz several times a year to minister to the town's rural population.
On Saturday he returned by helicopter, where he was greeted by singing and cheering. He later did a tour in a popemobile, where he waved to people who had travelled from across the region to see him.
Speaking at a local parish on Saturday, the Pope said he felt "joy" at being able to visit the small town once again.
"It is like a very big dream that the Lord has allowed this servant to come here," he said.
Rev. Kevin Noriega, who was ordained in 2018 by the then-bishop, told Reuters the visit had brought "enormous hope and emotion" to Santa Cruz.
He said: "People are eager to experience this Holy Mass ... because after so much time they will be able to see their bishop - 'Father Robert,' as they used to call him - now as the Holy Father."
Peru is the longest stop on the first tour of Latin America by the leader of the Catholic church, who was elected in May 2025.
The 12-day trip has included stops in Argentina and Uruguay, but his time in Peru carries personal significance.
The US-born pope not only lived in Peru for long periods between 1985 and 2023 but also became a citizen of the country in 2015, forging close ties with local communities.

The pontiff is set to leave Chiclayo on Sunday, when he will head to Cusco, and then on to a Peruvian sector of the Amazon rainforest. His tour of the region will conclude on Monday, at which point Pope Leo will return to Rome.

Carney toured the Minor Basilica and Metropolitan Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception, the official name of the Manila Cathedral, and Fort Santiago in the historic Intramuros district.

articles.title: Philippines, Australia ink updated defense cooperation deal
articles.summary: The Defense Cooperation Arrangement updates an earlier 1995 deal to serve as a ‘contemporary bilateral defense framework’ for the two countries

blocks.text: UPDATED PACT. Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, Philippine Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr., and Australian Ambassador to the Philippines Marc Innes-Brown at a signing ceremony for the Philippines-Australia Defense Cooperation Arrangement in Manila, November 15, 2026.
Hollie Adams/Reuters
The Defense Cooperation Arrangement updates an earlier 1995 deal to serve as a ‘contemporary bilateral defense framework’ for the two countries

MANILA, Philippines – Officials from the Philippines and Australia on Sunday, November 15, signed the Philippines-Australia Defense Cooperation Arrangement (DCA), an update to a 30-year-old agreement.

Philippine Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. and Australian Ambassador to the Philippines Marc Innes-Brown signed the agreement at the Manila South Harbor in the presence of Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese.
Albanese is in Manila for the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit and Related Summits.

The DCA, according to a joint statement by Teodoro and Australian Deputy Prime Minister and Defense Minister Richard Marles following a bilateral meeting last August, would “set the contemporary bilateral defense framework” from the 1995 Memorandum of Understanding on Defense Cooperation.

Manila and Canberra’s bilateral ties have grown closer under the Marcos administration. The two countries officially elevated ties to a strategic partnership in September 2023. In February 2024, Marcos addressed Australia’s parliament — an honor extended to only a handful of world leaders.

The two countries have had a Status of Visiting Forces Agreement since 2012, giving soldiers from both countries easier access to each other’s soil for training exercises and humanitarian response. The two militaries hold regular bilateral and multilateral drills and exercises, including in the West Philippine Sea.

Canberra is among Manila’s closest partners, particularly in trying to assert its entitlements in its exclusive economic zone in the South China Sea, which China claims as its territory. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Katherine Deves among four NSW upper house candidates revealed by One Nation
articles.summary:
Party’s NSW leader Mike Newman says contenders are ‘people from the real world’ and not ‘career politicians’

  • Get our

blocks.text: The failed federal Liberal candidate Katherine Deves, who campaigned to exclude transgender women from women’s sport, will stand for One Nation at next year’s New South Wales election.
Deves was among four NSW Legislative Council candidates announced by One Nation’s NSW leader, Mike Newman, on Sunday.

The other candidates were Arnon Wither, a construction worker from the Hunter region who works as an electorate officer for Senator Sean Bell; Manti Steele, a farmer, teacher and mother of eight from Dubbo; and Daniel Hill, a surf lifesaver from the state’s south coast.
The NSW election will be held on 13 March.
Newman said on Sunday the upper house candidates were “authentic”, “people from the real world” and not “career politicians”.
One Nation has only announced a single lower house candidate – Newman, in the electorate of Cessnock – but he said the party would run candidates in all 93 lower house seats.
“We want to make sure that these people bleed orange, and like I said, they’re all from the real world,” he said.

“That’s the that’s the type of person we’re aiming at … people from the real world who understand business, who understand their pinch points and pain points, understand the cost of living, understand cashflow.”

Deves was handpicked by the former prime minister Scott Morrison to run in the federal NSW seat of Warringah in 2022. Her candidacy was marred by controversy, including when she likened anti-trans activism to standing up against the Holocaust.
On Sunday she said she joined One Nation “because I wanted to be a part of the rescue, recovery, and restoration of our nation”.

“We are seeing cost of living skyrocket, whether it’s fuel, housing, energy, and we are watching a government that is so wedded to destructive ideologies like DEI and net zero that they are prepared to impoverish us all,” she said.
after newsletter promotion
If elected, she would look to make changes to state laws regarding “discrimination, hate speech, vilification, birth certificates, etc”.

“Where we can restore clear and accurate language around biological sex, men and women, and ensure that women and girls are safe and have spaces for services, sports, etc, where it’s inappropriate for males to be there.”
One Nation has required candidates at state elections to sign non-disclosure agreements preventing them from discussing their potential candidacy with the media.
News24 reported last month that Deves would run as an upper house candidate in the NSW election. She announced that she joined One Nation in September.

When Guardian Australia contacted Deves about her potential candidacy in October, she directed inquiries to Vikki Campion, the NSW party’s part-time media adviser. The party provided a statement saying it had confirmed only three candidates at that time – Newman, the lead upper house candidate, Stuart Bonds, and a Tamworth firearms manufacturer, Jeff Bacon.

articles.title: Keeping Ayala in the family: How the Zobels pass the torch
articles.summary: Can a summer in the unfamiliar Australian Outback prepare someone to lead a business empire? JAZA certainly seems to think so.

blocks.text: PILLARS. Ayala Corporation chairman Jaime Augusto Zobel de Ayala (center) and his son, ACMobility president and CEO Jaime Alfonso Zobel de Ayala (right), speak with Bath Spa University chancellor Sharanjit Leyl at the ASEAN Inclusive Growth Summit on Wednesday, November 11.
ASEAN Business Advisory Council Philippines
Can a summer in the unfamiliar Australian Outback prepare someone to lead a business empire? JAZA certainly seems to think so.

items: Jaime Augusto Zobel de Ayala, known as JAZA, was encouraged by his father to join the family business, leading to his current role as chairman of Ayala Corporation, a major Philippine conglomerate.
JAZA emphasizes the importance of resilience and problem-solving in parenting, sharing experiences of pushing his children outside their comfort zones to prepare them for future leadership roles.
As Ayala Corporation approaches its bicentennial in 2034, JAZA focuses on maintaining the company's relevance in a changing world while ensuring the next generation is equipped to lead.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
There was never any pressure on Jaime Augusto Zobel de Ayala to join the family business. So how did he end up leading one of the Philippines’ oldest and biggest business empires?
As it turns out, all it took was a little favor from his father, or more accurately, a series of little favors.

The elder Jaime Zobel de Ayala had financed his son’s education in the United States and encouraged him to find his own path in life. Along the way, Jaime Augusto, better known as JAZA, would also lend a hand whenever his father asked him to help out with this or that.
Then, one day, came a bigger request: Would he come home to the Philippines and work in the family business for just three years? After that, he was free to pursue whatever future he wanted.

“I enjoyed the challenges that the Philippines put on the table, working in an emerging market. I found it fantastic and very exciting, a chance to make a difference,” JAZA said. “The rest is history.”

blocks.caption: Keeping Ayala in the family: How the Zobels pass the torch

blocks.text: Decades later, he is chairman of Ayala Corporation, a nearly 200-year-old conglomerate whose businesses span banking, property, telecommunications, and energy.
And now, it is his turn to prepare the next generation of Zobels, including his son Jaime Alfonso Zobel de Ayala, better known as JAZ.
At the ASEAN Inclusive Growth Summit on Wednesday, November 11, father and son shared a few stories about growing up in a family that has been running businesses for nearly two centuries.

JAZA recalled sending his son, then just 13 or 14, to work on a farm in the Australian Outback, far from familiar faces and comforts. It was part of his parenting philosophy of pushing children outside their comfort zones.
“All of us have a responsibility to put people through difficult places at certain points in life to try and build up a sense of resilience, a sense of problem solving,” JAZA said.
His son remembers things a little differently.
“JAZA has never liked me hanging around during the summer,” JAZ joked, recalling that his time in the Outback also involved “a lot of horseback riding.”
And yes, he calls his father JAZA, even when sharing family stories. “It’s his name in the office. Hard to say ‘Dad,’” JAZ said, drawing chuckles from the crowd.
In any case, JAZA said he had “no kind of formal plan” when it came to preparing his children. What mattered was teaching them to find solutions rather than complain about their circumstances.
Time will tell whether these lessons will play out as the next generation of Zobels take their posts in the conglomerate.
JAZ now heads ACMobility, Ayala’s automotive and electric mobility arm. His sister Mariana Zobel de Ayala oversees Ayala Land’s leasing and hospitality businesses.

Their cousins Jaime Zobel Urquijo and Paloma Zobel de Ayala are also involved in the group, part of another generation preparing to carry the nearly 200-year-old institution forward. (READ: Preparing for the future: Ayala promotes 4 ‘next-generation’ leaders)

But succession at Ayala isn’t just about keeping executive titles in the family. Career executives have played a central role, with JAZ crediting his father for empowering them to lead. At BPI, for instance, JAZA remains chairman even as the bank prepares to hand over its presidency from TG Limcaoco to Ginbee Go in April 2027.

blocks.caption: Bigger bank, broader base: TG Limcaoco’s BPI years

blocks.text: Ayala traces its beginnings to 1834 and will celebrate its bicentennial in 2034. Having survived Spanish and American colonial rule, two world wars, and countless economic crises, the conglomerate has seen more than its share of history.
But for JAZA, more important than holding on to its storied legacy is ensuring that the nearly 200-year-old institution is still relevant.
“Remaining relevant to the changing nature of the country and the world is vitally important,” JAZA said.
“I always wanted an Ayala that was important to the country in a broader sense and touching the lives of as many Filipinos as possible.” – Rappler.com

articles.title: Thunderstorms, giant hail and powerful winds forecast for NSW as wild weather hits east coast
articles.summary:
Volatile weather predicted after storms on Saturday, with a man in his 20s struck by lightning while swimming on NSW Central Coast

  • Get our

blocks.text: Dangerous and severe “supercell” thunderstorms with the potential for giant hail and destructive winds were forecast for parts of New South Wales on Sunday, as volatile weather continued in the eastern states over the weekend.

Storms dumped heavy rain across large parts of northern and eastern NSW and much of Queensland on Saturday, with strong winds recorded up to 98km/h in Goulburn and rainfall totals of between 30mm and 50mm in the Coffs Harbour area.

A man in his 20s was struck by lightning while swimming at Ettalong beach on NSW’s Central Coast on Saturday afternoon. He was pulled from the water by fellow swimmers and given CPR by first responders until NSW Ambulance paramedics arrived. He was taken to Gosford hospital in a serious condition, and later transferred to Royal North Shore hospital.
The young man was in a critical but stable condition on Sunday morning, a hospital spokesperson said.
Witnesses said while there was storm activity visible in the distance towards Gosford, the area around the beach was clear and sunny and that the lightning bolt appeared to come “out of nowhere”.
Lightning can strike up to 30km from the centre of a storm cell.
Sunday was expected to be “another big storm day”, with “very dangerous and severe thunderstorms” likely for north-eastern NSW, said Sarah Scully, senior meteorologist at the Bureau of Meteorology.

blocks.caption: Authorities attend the scene after a man in his 20s was struck by lightning while swimming at  Ettalong beach on the NSW Central Coast on Saturday. Photograph: 9 News

blocks.text: Those storms could bring hail with a diameter greater than 5cm, and winds in excess of 120km/h.
“That’s being driven by a southerly change that’s pushing up the New South Wales coast,” Scully said. “It’s a potential trigger for these supercell high-end thunderstorms.”

Severe thunderstorms with 2cm hail, wind gusts in excess of 90km/h, heavy rainfall and flash flooding was possible on Sunday through a broader area of NSW extending down towards inland parts of the ranges to the east of Sydney, and pushing up into south-east and central parts of Queensland.

Storms were expected in Sydney on Sunday, but were likely to be less severe than further north, though rain was likely. The forecast temperature was 23C. Showers and thunderstorms were expected in Brisbane with a top of 31C.
The BoM expected to release more severe weather warnings throughout Sunday as the storms develop.
after newsletter promotion

On Monday, the risk of high-end severe thunderstorms would move into the NSW northern rivers and south-eastern parts of Queensland, including Brisbane, the Gold Coast and the Sunshine Coast, again with the potential to bring giant hail, destructive winds, and intense rain that could lead to life-threatening flash flooding.
“That again is being driven by that trough that’s pushing up the coast combined with the very humid conditions that eastern Australia has been experiencing the last few days,” Scully said.
A coastal trough with a low-pressure system appeared to be developing off the north coast of NSW near the Queensland border, which had the potential to bring even more rain onto the coast.
“How much rainfall accumulates is highly dependent on how close that trough sits to the coast, and also how long it lingers there,” Scully said.

“At this state we’re only expecting moderate rainfall totals during tomorrow from that coastal trough, between 30mm to 70mm, easing into Tuesday morning. But we are watching it very closely as rainfall totals associated with these coastal troughs are notoriously challenging to predict. If they just move that little bit closer to the coast they can sometimes dump a whole lot of rain.”

Elsewhere, there were showers developing in Melbourne on Sunday with a forecast top of 17C. There was a high chance of showers in Hobart, with 13C expected, and cloudy in Adelaide with a mild 20C forecast. It was partly cloudy in Canberra, where they were expecting 24C, and in Perth, with an expected top of 28C. Darwin was expecting 34C and an afternoon storm.

articles.title: Marcos creates national AI council, adopts governance framework
articles.summary: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has signed an executive order adopting a national framework for artificial intelligence governance and creating an inter-agency council to oversee its implementation.

blocks.text: November 15, 2026 | 9:00am
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. meets with Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on the sidelines of the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits in the Philippines on Nov. 14, 2026.
Presidential Communications Office via Facebook

MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has signed an executive order adopting a national framework for artificial intelligence (AI) governance and creating an inter-agency council to oversee its implementation.
Palace press officer Claire Castro announced on Saturday, November 14, that Marcos signed Executive Order No. 131 on November 12.
The order adopts the AI Governance Framework as a guide for policy formulation, regulatory coordination, institutional development and capacity-building.

It also establishes the National Artificial Intelligence Council (NAIC), which will coordinate, facilitate and monitor the implementation of the framework among government agencies and other stakeholders.

The NAIC will be an inter-agency body chaired by the executive secretary, with representatives from other government agencies, including the Department of Economy, Planning and Development and the Commission on Higher Education.
The order seeks to establish a unified direction for AI development and ensure its responsible, safe and ethical use, with safeguards to protect public trust.

“Sa pamamagitan ng kautusan na ito ng pangulo, binibigyang-halaga nito ang AI upang mapabuti ang buhay ng mga Pilipino hindi lamang para isulong ang teknolohiya,” Castro said during a briefing at the International Media Center in Pasay City.
(Through this executive order, the president recognizes the importance of AI in improving the lives of Filipinos, not merely in advancing technology.)
“Layunin nitong tiyakin na ang AI ay maipapatupad nang responsable, ligtas, ethical, at may sapat na proteksyon upang mapanatili ang tiwala ng publiko,” she added.
(Its goal is to ensure that AI is implemented responsibly, safely and ethically, with adequate safeguards to maintain public trust.)
Castro said the measure aims to ensure that AI development benefits workers, businesses and communities, as well as the country as a whole.
Earlier on Saturday, Marcos called on businesses across Southeast Asia to make AI tools more affordable and accessible to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).

In a video message to the Association of Southeast Asian Nations Business and Investment Summit 2026, the president said small businesses should have access to technology that would help them compete in an increasingly digital economy.
“For MSMEs, we are advancing an approach that brings AI adoption together with training and practical support,” Marcos said.
“Our aim is to help entrepreneurs spend less time on repetitive tasks, make better use of their resources, and reach more customers,” he added.
A copy of EO No. 131 has yet to be published on the Official Gazette website.

articles.title: Tens of thousands continue to protest across France
articles.summary: Some 106,000 people marched through French cities for a fifth consecutive weekend of protests, marking the lowest turnout in recent weeks.

image.caption: Protests that began over underfunded schools have since spread to wider public grievancesImage: Benoit Tessier/REUTERS

blocks.text: Tens of thousands of protesters took to the streets across France on Saturday to demonstrate against the rising cost of living and strained public services, the Interior Ministry said.

Saturday's demonstrations drew their lowest turnout in recent weeks. Some 106,000 people marched through French cities, with 24,000 in Paris alone. The previous weekend, some 146,000 people had participated nationwide.
The number of arrests was also significantly lower. Police detained 219 people across the country, according to the Interior Ministry.
Although the demonstrations were largely peaceful, police fired tear gas in Paris, Bordeaux and the western city of Nantes, including after some protesters shot fireworks.
French business owners share harrowing accounts of violent protests
France's protests expose deeper anger
Mass protests have swept across the European Union's second-largest economy for more than a month.

What began in September as student protests against teacher shortages and poor facilities has since evolved into a broader movement fuelled by anger over the rising cost of living, strained public services and police brutality.
In mid-October, around 565,000 people took to the streets across France, as riots, looting and clashes disrupted demonstrations in several cities.
As France entered its fifth consecutive weekend of nationwide unrest, President Emmanuel Macron's approval ratings fell to the lowest level since he took office in 2017, according to recent polls.
The French government doesn't have much room to respond to the protesters' demands due to its high debt.

articles.title: What can PH benefit from hosting ASEAN Summit? Geopolitical analyst explains
articles.summary: The financial cost of hosting the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits has been considerable for the Philippines, but a geopolitical analyst said Sunday that accommodating global leaders could…

blocks.text: Published November 15, 2026 8:49am

The financial cost of hosting the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits has been considerable for the Philippines, but a geopolitical analyst said Sunday that accommodating global leaders could benefit the country in return.
Geopolitical analyst Dindo Manhit said the ASEAN Summit is an opportunity for the member states from the Southeast Asia region to cooperate with each other.

"Siguro tignan natin sa konteksto na isa tayo sa mga founding members ng ASEAN… Ngayon ay 11 na tayo at ito ay nagpapakita ng unity in diversity. Kahit papaano ang iba't-ibang bansa, at least nakakapagusap-usap, nakakapagtulungan," he told Super Radyo dzBB.

(Perhaps let's look at it in the context that we are one of the founding members of ASEAN... Now there are 11 of us, and this is a display of unity in diversity. Somehow, the different countries are at least able to talk and help one other.)
ASEAN was established on August 8, 1967 in Bangkok, Thailand with the signing of the ASEAN Declaration by Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand as its founding members.
The organization later welcomed Brunei Darussalam in 1984. Vietnam joined in 1995, while Laos and Myanmar came into the picture in 1997. Cambodia joined its ranks in 1999.
Timor Leste was the latest country to join the regional bloc in 2025.
But Manhit said the hosting of the ASEAN Summit actually exposes the Philippines to countries outside of the region.

"Ang kagandahan lang dito, ang ASEAN - hindi man siya perpekto - ito ay pagkakataon ng isang bansa tulad ng Pilipinas na makilala, makausap ng ibang bansa labas sa ASEAN. Malakas ang ASEAN, ‘yung kanilang tinatawag na drawing power," he said.

(What is good about this is that ASEAN— even if it isn't perfect— is an opportunity for a country like the Philippines to be recognized and to talk to other countries outside ASEAN. ASEAN is strong, with what is called "drawing power.")
"Dumadating rin ‘yung mga bisita natin with the promise of partnership, promise of economic investment," he added.
(Our visitors also arrive with the promise of partnership, [and the] promise of economic investment.)
Ahead of the summit, the Philippines and Canada have concluded negotiations for a free trade agreement (FTA), with both countries aiming to sign the pact in 2027.
Meanwhile, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva have discussed strengthening agricultural cooperation to protect local farms and support food security.
Marcos earlier said that the hosting of the ASEAN summit "is an important opportunity to create more jobs, support local businesses and open new doors for our people."

The government has allocated P22.9 billion for the ASEAN Summit, as it marks its fifth time to chair the regional bloc. But the Palace said it is ready to have the cost of being the event’s host be audited. —RF, GMA News

articles.title: UK government to consider changing age of consent after allegations against Russell Brand
articles.summary:
Deputy prime minister says change would be a massive step but ‘deserves proper consideration and scrutiny’

The government has said it will consider calls to change the age of consent after…

blocks.text: The government has said it will consider calls to change the age of consent after a woman waived her right to anonymity to publicly claim she was raped by Russell Brand as a 16-year-old schoolgirl.
Mia Latter, now 37, alleged she had been orally raped by the jailed comedian when she was a teenager and he was 30 years old.
In an interview with the Sunday Times, she called for the introduction of a staggered age of consent – which would make relationships between adults and teenagers aged 16 and 17 illegal.
Louise Haigh, the de facto deputy prime minister, told the newspaper that Latter’s “heart-breaking story” meant a law change deserved consideration.

She said: “We need to listen to Mia and other victims like her who have been through these experiences because it’s really important that as lawmakers their experience is at the heart of what we consider.
“It clearly would be a massive step to change the age of consent, but it deserves proper consideration and scrutiny. I can absolutely understand why she is calling for it.”
Under UK law, adults of any age are legally able to have sex with 16 and 17-year-olds.
Latter said: “It’s shocking to me time and time again that whenever the news comes up again about him, it’s always in the comments about the relationship with a 16-year-old.

“That’s not the most heinous bit. But why is that the thing that everybody collectively gets stuck on? I think we all sort of agree that … adults shouldn’t be allowed to have sexual relationships with children, with somebody under the age of 18. That really doesn’t seem like a gigantic leap to take.”
Latter was referred to under the pseudonym of Alice in previous reporting by the Sunday Times, the Times, and Channel 4’s Dispatches documentary.
She was 16 when she first met Brand in Leicester Square, central London, while she was on her way home from a shopping trip.
He took her number and later messaged her, asking if she wanted to go for dinner, she said.
She told the newspaper that Brand – who was working at MTV at the time – still asked her to meet after she had confessed her age to him.
Latter alleges Brand orally raped her towards the end of their three-month relationship.
Brand denied all of the allegations made against him by Latter when they were first reported in 2023 by the Times.
She spoke to the police after the documentary, but the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) decided not to include her case in Brand’s trial at Southwark Crown Court.
He was convicted of attacks against four of the six women who gave evidence against him, and is now serving a 10-and-a-half-year prison term for one count of rape and three sexual assaults.

Earlier this week, it was announced that a series of “serious” sex offence allegations against comedian David Walliams are being probed by the Metropolitan police after an investigation by the Guardian and ITV News.
One woman described her alleged encounter with Walliams when she was 15 as “sexual assault”.
Walliams denies any wrongdoing.

Haigh went on to say that, in light of news that one of Walliams’s accusers was asked to sign a non disclosure agreement (NDA), the government should also look at banning them in cases of alleged sexual assault and harassment. She said: “When we consider the allegations against David Walliams, teenagers who were fans wouldn’t come under the current consultation.

“I do think there is a very strong case to look at banning NDAs in all circumstances where they relate to harassment or discrimination, to make sure that no victim, regardless of where it happened or what their relationship was with the perpetrator, should ever be silenced.”
It is believed MPs outside Labour may support a bill to change the age of consent laws, with Jess Brown-Fuller, the Liberal Democrat justice spokesperson, coming out in favour of reviewing them.

Commending Latter for the “extraordinary bravery” it took to waive her anonymity, Brown-Fuller said: “I think we must go further to increase protections for young women and girls, and looking at a staggered age of consent is an important step.

“We already have rules that recognise power imbalances in professions: between teachers and students, or barristers and junior colleagues. It’s time for the government to recognise the implicit power imbalance held by older men over teenage girls.”

Latter’s decision to come forward was also praised by Bridget Phillipson, the minister for women and equalities, who said she “and thousands of others across the country will be in awe of her courage and determination”. She added that it is “up to all of us to send a message to women and girls who experience sexual violence: the shame is not yours. Women like Mia are leading the charge, but we can and must do more to make this a moment of change.”
Latter’s allegation was reported to the Met police, who said the investigation into the alleged rape remains ongoing.
A Met Police spokesperson said: “Officers launched an investigation in January 2026 after receiving an allegation of rape.
“Detectives sought advice from the Crown Prosecution Service to determine how best to proceed, and officers were advised that further information was needed before a charging decision could be made.
“This investigation remains ongoing. We understand the delay has been distressing for this victim-survivor. However, our focus has been on putting forward the best possible evidence.”
The CPS said: “The Crown Prosecution Service will continue to work closely with investigators to provide advice and make sure cases progress as quickly as possible.”

articles.title: My mother told me I would die if I sought treatment for Ebola - I am proof you can survive
articles.summary: Fear and misinformation surrounds the Ebola outbreak in DR Congo - Dr Kamwanga's mother was not immune.

blocks.text: My mother told me I would die if I sought treatment for Ebola - I am proof you can survive
Image source, Braton Serge/BBC
ByRuth Alonga
BBC AfricaReporting fromButembo

When Dr Raymond Kasereka Kamwanga told his family he suspected he had Ebola and was going to a treatment centre in the city of Butembo in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, his family were horrified.

They regarded the specialised unit as a "death house" as not many patients do recover - especially those admitted in the late stages of the illness. His 50-year-old mother was in tears, pleading with him not to go there.
"Why are you choosing to die at the Ebola treatment centre?" Masika Ndungo had asked him.
But as a doctor at Butembo's Katwa Hospital, he knew that if stayed at home, he was unlikely to survive.

This was in July, two months after the World Health Organization (WHO) had declared the Ebola outbreak in DR Congo a public health emergency of international concern. Since then 5,400 people have died and 11,000 have been infected, making it the second-most deadly outbreak ever recorded.
Butembo is in North Kivu province, the epicentre of the crisis, with the highest number of reported cases, according to the Congolese health ministry.
Dr Kamwanga is one of 3,031 people who have survived - and is evangelical about sharing his story in an effort to help stop the spread of infections devastating his community.
After staring death in the face and overcoming ostracisation, he has even started writing a book about his experience.
"As someone who has recovered, I am living proof that the disease exists, but also that it is possible to recover from it," he tells the BBC outside Katwa Hospital where he still works.
The 30-year-old medic believes he contracted the virus through contact with a patient in a setting where protective measures are not always adequate.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Raymond Kasereka Kamwanga uses his book to help convince sceptics that Ebola is real

blocks.text: Raymond Kasereka Kamwanga uses his book to help convince sceptics that Ebola is real
The first symptoms appeared gradually: a bitter taste in his mouth, headaches and a general feeling of malaise. He contacted the Ebola response team.
After an initial consultation and some tests, he returned home, but his condition did not improve.
Butembo does not have the equipment to quickly test for Ebola - samples need to be sent to the city of Beni, 54km (33 miles) north.
This delays diagnosis as the condition of roads in this war-torn and underdeveloped part of DR Congo means it can take between 48 and 72 hours to travel even this relatively short distance.
After three days at home, Kamwanga felt extremely weak and experienced muscle pain. On the fourth day, he began vomiting and had diarrhoea.
This is when he gathered his family members - including his mother - to tell them he had to go to the Ebola treatment centre.
"She had started crying, along with my sisters. I told them everything would be alright, that I was a doctor and that I was confident. But they weren't reassured," he says.
Around 18:00, he set off on foot to the nearby centre but refused to use the main entrance.

He called his colleagues and asked them to put on their protective gear before they approached him and isolated him. The virus spreads from one person to another by contact with infected bodily fluids.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Dr Kamwanga's mother says his experience has helped dispel some of the misinformation she had heard about Ebola

blocks.text: Dr Kamwanga's mother says his experience has helped dispel some of the misinformation she had heard about Ebola
The current outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo species of the virus for which there is no approved vaccine or treatment.
"The treatment given to Ebola patients is symptomatic - meaning that doctors treat the symptoms the patient presents," says Kamwanga, explaining that in his case it was severe vomiting and diarrhoea.
In some patients these symptoms can lead to organ failure and then some develop internal and external bleeding.
Kamwanga lost a lot of fluid and struggled to stay hydrated - he was terrified.
"I was afraid for myself. Every day, patients were dying right before my eyes. But I stayed positive," he explains.
Over 13 days lying in his hospital bed, he tried to keep his spirits up by watching movies and TV shows on his phone, reading and scrolling through TikTok.
The day he learned he had recovered, Kamwanga felt immense relief. He thanked the healthcare workers who had cared for him.
However, even a certificate showing he was Ebola-free did not initially dispel the unease those around him felt after he was discharged.
"We welcomed him home warmly. But because of our fear, we didn't get close to him any more," Ndungo, his mother, tells the BBC.

For 21 days - the incubation period of the virus - the doctor lived separately in another part of the family home, which was crowded at the time with at least 18 people living there, including several children and people displaced by recent fighting in the region.
He would only see them from afar when he went to pick up his meal, while other family members kept their distance.
Neighbour Kavugho Sifa shared these concerns.
"We were really afraid, but we prayed to God to protect him at the treatment centre. With God's help and the doctors' efforts, we saw him return in good health," she tells the BBC.
They all agree the experience changed their perception of Ebola.

blocks.caption: Graphic showing how Ebola attacks the human body, sourced to the WHO and Cleveland Clinic. Graphic showing how Ebola systematically attacks the human body. It explains that symptoms appear two to 21 days after contact and can worsen over time. Earlier symptoms, shown with purple circles around di…

blocks.text: Some do not believe the disease even exists - Ndungo says that witnessing Ebola first-hand helped to dispel some of that misinformation.
After his recovery, Kamwanga threw himself into community outreach - sharing his story as a way of combatting rumours and mistrust.

"I started writing my book - The Price of Saving Lives - one week after recovering and leaving the hospital," he says. "However, it is not finished yet. What I currently use during my awareness-raising activities is the draft, and it is already making a significant impact."
During these sessions, he also distributes photos taken while he was sick to help convince residents that Ebola is real.
But in Butembo, this mission remains difficult. Kamwanga explains that some people view awareness campaigns as a way for humanitarian organisations to profit from donor funding.
Such mistrust, which is also levelled at healthcare professionals, is often fuelled by poverty and trauma related to years of armed conflict, he says.

"Ebola has come alongside the war," he says, explaining that some even interpret it as a way for those in authority to threaten a vulnerable population "to finish off those whom the war failed to exterminate".
He also believes that the number of deaths observed during epidemics - compared to recoveries, which are sometimes less visible - reinforce fear and suspicion.
But putting himself on the front line also comes with risks - and Kamwanga says he receives death threats on his phone.
Some residents accuse him of being paid to spread information about Ebola. He also reports that outreach workers have been attacked by members of the community.
He feels the authorities do not work effectively to address all these problems: "Our government is taking things lightly."
He agrees too with the recent report by Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) that Ebola funds are going missing.
"The money allocated to the Ebola response is being misappropriated by the government. We do not have enough protective equipment," the medic says.
The BBC has asked the Congolese government for comment.
Despite the intimidation and the obstacles he and other medics face, he remains determined - his goal is to help put an end to the disease.
"Should we give up the fight against Ebola? No. We continue to do what we can with the resources available to us, which are unfortunately very limited."

articles.title: Judo champion shakes up French presidential race with surprise candidacy
articles.summary: Teddy Riner is one of the most popular figures in modern-day France, and one in five voters say they could support him.

blocks.text: Image source, Reuters
Five-times Olympic champion Teddy Riner is one of France's most popular athletes
Apart from an overwhelming urge to pin one's opponent to the floor of the house, there is no obvious connection between politics and the world of top-level judo.
That has not stopped France's much-garlanded world heavyweight champion Teddy Riner from throwing his hat into the ring for next April's presidential race.

The Guadeloupe-born 37-year-old may have no experience of public office, no party behind him, and as yet no manifesto. All so far is a slogan La France qu'on aime (The France we love), a declaration on social media, and a campaign visit to a hospital in the Seine-Saint-Denis suburb of northern Paris.
But it would be a foolhardy pundit who would totally write off his chances.

Riner is, after all, one of the most popular figures in modern-day France, regularly topping the polls for embodying the nation's "values". He is a proven winner, with five Olympic golds and 11 world championships under his belt, as well as a successful career in business.

More than 28 million people have watched his election broadcast on Instagram and X, shot with proper presidential decorum against a backdrop of books and a French flag. Some 22% told an Ifop poll within 24 hours they "could" vote for him.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Teddy Riner's video has attracted 14.5 million views on Instagram alone

blocks.text: Image source, Getty Images
Teddy Riner's video has attracted 14.5 million views on Instagram alone
Actors and television personalities have become presidents in other countries. The ex-leader of Liberia – George Weah – was formerly a professional footballer.
So why not a judoka in the Élysée Palace?
"Anyone who thinks that being out of the political in-crowd disqualifies Riner from running for the Élysée would be very wrong," says Guillaume Tabard of Le Figaro.
"But [Riner] too would be wrong if he thinks not belonging to the in-crowd is all it takes."

For now the whole of the French political world has decided to take the Riner candidacy seriously – or at least to pretend to. That is partly because he is such a popular personality that mocking his political hopes could easily rebound badly.
But it is also because the state of French politics – outside of the burgeoning forces of the hard left and hard right – is one of total disarray.

The centre-ground is floundering, with no candidate yet emerging who can inspire anything like the sense of mission of hard-right leader Marine Le Pen and Jean-Luc Mélenchon on the hard left, who for now look set to face off in the final round of the presidential election in May.

So when a popular figure like Riner enters the race - proclaiming himself "neither left, nor right", wanting to "unite the country" and "put money back in people's pockets", railing equally against "racists" and "yobs who scare people off our streets" – politicians have to take note.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Hard-right leader Marine Le Pen currently leads the polls in the race to be France's next president

blocks.text: Hard-right leader Marine Le Pen currently leads the polls in the race to be France's next president

It is perfectly possible, probable even, that Riner's campaign will fizzle out after a brief period of hype, and that the judoka will after all be a joker in the pack. But it is also possible that it won't, in which case the pre-election arithmetic will need a hasty readjustment: and it won't be the centrists who are smiling.
Thus far, Riner has shown himself a master of the codes required for this kind of out-of-nowhere candidacy, the first of which is to press home the message: "Don't Worry! I'm NOT a Politician!"

In this day and age in France, anyone who smacks of the "system" is automatically downgraded in voters' eyes, so it is important to emphasise that you are only running for office because, one, you have experienced real life (unlike those loafers in Paris); and two, you have discovered that there are solutions out there for the country's many problems. Solutions that are invisible to those same blinkered apparatchiks.
All this Riner was able to express in last Monday's social media broadcast by using sophisticated rhetorical devices.
"People say I am a fool for wanting to run for the presidency," he said.

"Am I a fool? Well, if refusing to see France sink under the weight of debt; refusing to see mothers and fathers grit their teeth every time they do their weekly shop, and tremble with fear when their kids go out on the street… if all that means being a fool, then yes call me a fool."
It was a promising oratorial start for the sportsman, and certainly attracted the viewers.
But if he is serious – and Riner says he never does anything half-heartedly - that's not how he became an Olympic champion – then the hard work begins now.

What does Riner actually want to do? Who will be on his team? Where does he position himself on the all-consuming matters of the day: pension-reform, investment in education, the cost of living, public debt, the rise of populism or Russia's war in Ukraine?
In short, how does he intend to transform his undeniable popularity as a sporting figure into a political mandate?

blocks.caption: Image caption, Protesters have for weeks taken to the streets in France over wages, the cost of living and public services

blocks.text: Protesters have for weeks taken to the streets in France over wages, the cost of living and public services

Broadly, Riner appears to be on the right on economic matters and law and order, but being black and of Caribbean background he is also very strong on racism. When he says he is anti-extremism, he is referring mainly to Marine Le Pen.
In other words his pitch is somewhere in the centre, and against the extremes.
The trouble is, this is already an extremely crowded area, with important figures like ex-prime ministers Edouard Philippe and Gabriel Attal signally failing to take off.

Currently there are a dozen or so candidates in the area between centre right and centre left, stretching from the Socialist-backed Raphaël Glucksman to the Republicans' Bruno Retailleau on the right.
The latest possible addition is Christine Lagarde, who steps down as head of the European Central Bank next February.

blocks.caption: Image caption, President Emmanuel Macron is among the few politicians who appears genuinely pleased by Riner's decision to run

blocks.text: Image source, Pool/AFP via Getty Images
President Emmanuel Macron is among the few politicians who appears genuinely pleased by Riner's decision to run
The addition of yet another contender will dilute their polling numbers even further, making a second-round qualification for Mélenchon more likely.
So no wonder the leader of France Unbowed (LFI) seemed so happy about Riner's decision to run. "We know how it goes: neither right nor left means not left," Mélenchon told reporters on Friday.

The only other politician who seems genuinely pleased, rather than putting on a fixed smile, is President Emmanuel Macron, who said Riner was a "great champion" and that politics "did not belong to the professionals".

That could be explained by the president's cool relations with his former prime ministers, Philippe and Attal, both of whom are doing all they can to distance themselves from their unpopular one-time boss.
Riner said he viewed Macron's praise as a "poisoned chalice", telling reporters on Saturday that he was "not the president's envoy, I'm not a Macronist".

Politics and judo have very little in common, but of the two, as Riner will soon discover, the more vicious is not the one that is fought out hand-to-hand after mutual acknowledgement on the tatami mat.
In Japanese, judo actually means "the gentle way".
If he starts looking like a serious candidate, Riner must know his life will be turned upside down, not just his physical form.
In politics you do not bow in respect to your opponent. You give him a metaphorical headbutt.
