articles.title: US air travel slowly recovers from nationwide flight ground stop as chaos continues
articles.summary:
Thousands of flights still canceled as officials blamed ageing air control system for nationwide grounding

Travel chaos continued across the US on Saturday morning as airlines scrambled to…

blocks.text: Travel chaos continued across the US on Saturday morning as airlines scrambled to recover from a four-hour nationwide Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ground stop that delayed or canceled thousands of the flights.
On Saturday morning, more than 3,000 flights within, into or out of the US had already been canceled, according to FlightAware.
The longest nationwide group stop in 25 years left passengers stranded at airports across the country, with no certainty about exactly when they may reach their intended destination.

The US transportation secretary, Sean Duffy, on Friday blamed the ground stop on an ageing air control system, saying that the air traffic communications equipment became “overloaded with data and … they started to give us inconsistency in the data from those routers”.
“Because of that, we shut the system down,” the Trump administration official said.
The US homeland security secretary, Markwayne Mullin, said on Friday that there was “no indication as of yet” that the communications failure had been caused by “a nefarious attack against us”.
Duffy warned that it would “take us time” to “resume normal operations”.
“Our top priority is the safety of you and your family when you fly,” he said.
The rare flight grounding caused widespread disruptions, throwing travel plans into disarray as more than 8,000 flights across the country were canceled on Friday.

Among those affected by the fallout from the ground stop were sports teams traveling for games over the weekend. In college football, the Southeastern Conference announced that Mississippi’s game against Oklahoma had been rescheduled to Sunday – a day usually reserved for the National Football League (NFL).
Meanwhile, a men’s college basketball game between the University of North Carolina Greensboro and Cornell University, scheduled for Saturday, was postponed.

And although flights began resuming after the FAA’s decision to lift the ground stop, the aftermath still appears to be affecting passengers around the country. There were reported flight disruptions at airports in major cities including Boston, Washington DC, New York and Miami.

In a statement on Saturday, Duffy said that “operations are slowly returning to normal this morning” – but he added that “you will continue to see some delays and cancellations as carriers reschedule flights and reposition aircraft/crews where they are needed most”.
“Our top priority right now is making sure travelers get home safely to their families as quickly as possible,” he said.
Duffy said he planned to hold a news briefing at 10.30am ET.

The UK Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) also issued a statement on Saturday morning warning that “while US flights have resumed, there may be some follow-on disruption as airlines work to re-book affected passengers and get all services back to normal”.
The statement added: “Anyone due to travel on flights between the UK and USA should check with their airline for the latest information before heading to the airport.”

During the news briefing on Friday evening, Trump administration officials urged Congress – which until January is controlled by the White House’s Republican allies – to “fully fund a full build of a brand new air traffic control system”.

Friday marked the third nationwide ground stop issued by the FAA this century. The first occurred after the 11 September 2001 terrorist attacks. And the second took place in January 2023, after a pilot notification system went down.

articles.title: How a US extradition bid over Hamas allegations put a wealthy activist before a Spanish court
articles.summary:
James ‘Fergie’ Chambers, a Cox Enterprises heir, faced a two-hour hearing about alleged support for Hamas

A two-hour hearing in Spain’s high court Friday on the US extradition request of…

blocks.text: A two-hour hearing in Spain’s high court Friday on the US extradition request of wealthy leftwing activist and philanthropist James “Fergie” Chambers turned out to be a study in contrasts.

Chambers’s defense took most of the session to query the US citizen and detail irregularities in the Trump administration’s extradition request – several of which the Guardian has reported on – as well as the figures of Spanish law that would lead the three-judge panel to deny the request; while the prosecutor sped through his case, head down, asking Chambers no questions at all.

Notably, neither the judges or the prosecutor asked Chambers to address the insinuation in the extradition request that the wealthy activist had supported Hamas. Chambers’s case is the first known instance of the US seeking to extradite a citizen over alleged support for Hamas, an accusation apparently tied to an international money laundering charge and donations to organizations helping Palestinians in Gaza.

But the defense’s queries did allow him to speak for the first time since his 10 July arrest in Ibiza about events at the center of the case: 2023 protests against Israeli weapons manufacturer Elbit in Massachusets and New Hampshire and 2024 transfers of $7.2m to Tunisia, where he lived at the time. The latter was buttressed with testimony from a financial expert.

On the whole, Chambers painted a picture different from the depiction contained in the extradition request, that of a violent backer of Hamas on the run from the US. At one point, he noted that his family’s next door neighbor in Tunis was the US ambassador.

The court will decide next week on extraditing Chambers. If the decision is affirmative, Spain’s council of ministers can reverse the court’s decision. This means Chambers’s extradition may be among the last decisions made under Pedro Sánchez, the socialist prime minister, before national elections on 29 November.

Friday’s hearing began with Chambers’s defense asking about his wealth. A self-described communist and anti-imperialist, Chambers sold stock back to his family’s business, Atlanta-based Cox Enterprises, worth about $250m in mid-2023.

Then he started a foundation, he told the court. He and the foundation’s three-member board decide on funding and ensure that no projects seeking support are under US sanctions, Chambers said. The foundation has funded an estimated 100 progressive and humanitarian projects in 20 countries, according to his partner, activist and actor Stella Schnabel – including, Chambers said Friday, organizations in Gaza working on issues such as “medical treatment for children, transportation out of dangerous areas and clean water and food”.
Two of the request’s three charges – riot and conspiracy to riot – are related to the late-2023 protests against Elbit.

Chambers detailed his participation in the protests: locking himself to a door, marching in the street and – in New Hampshire – standing in the road, speaking to the media and paying bail for four protesters who were eventually found guilty of misdemeanor charges and served 30 days in jail.

As for the $7.2m, the defense and a financial expert serving as a witness laid out how ten bank transfers from the US to Tunisia mostly went to sponsor the football club Club Africain – described by Chambers as “one of the largest football clubs in Africa” – and a sporting business Chambers launched while living in Tunisia.
“Is there any indication that the money went to support terrorist activities?” asked defense attorney Aitor Martínez. “None,” said financial expert Albert Deulofeu Schilt.

Then, in about 15 minutes of rapid-fire monotone, prosecutor Juan Hernández Villalba laid out a wholly different picture of Chambers as backing “an organized structure … aimed at repeatedly committing illegal acts … together with funds destined for terrorist organizations”.
He accused the defense of laying out the facts of the case “in a fragmented way … when what’s most relevant is an evaluation of the whole picture”.
“The extradition petition isn’t based on ideology or political statements, but on actions [Chambers] organized, financed and carried out, causing material damage,” Hernández Villalba asserted.
The actions against Elbit “were presented as a simple protest”, he said. “Nevertheless, the actions described by the US were planned for days … with objectively violent content.”
Given all this, the prosecutor said, “there are more than enough indications to consider … that [Chambers’s] funding was aimed at terrorism”.

Among the 100-plus people in varying time zones following Friday’s hearing on the court’s YouTube channel was Irish film-maker and journalist Sinéad O’Shea, whose documentary on Chambers called All About the Money makes its New York premiere this weekend. It covers the time period cited by the FBI affidavit underpinning the US request. O’Shea said that extradition case “builds a false narrative which begins with the protest in New Hampshire – a piece of vandalism at worst and for which people ended up serving 30 days. I saw myself the football club in which he invested in Tunisia and his donations to Palestinian and other charities are a matter of public record. It is impossible not to see this as a politically motivated case.”

Chambers’s views have been extensively profiled in US media. A week after the 7 October 2023 Hamas attacks on Israel, he posted on X about Israel’s response: “Stop calling it ‘collective punishment’/There’s nothing to be ‘punished’ for/No faction of the Palestinian resistance, Hamas or other, has done *anything* wrong/It’s simply genocide/Like it has been.”
Dressed in dark jeans, a grey-blue shirt, a black jacket, with a close-cropped haircut and mustache, Chambers got the last word during the hearing.
“To this day I cannot understand why I have been in prison since July for what amounts to speaking emotionally and committing minor offenses of public disturbance,” he said.

“I’ve never had any contact with any terrorist organization. I’ve certainly never financed any terrorist organization … and for this my family has been torn apart. I missed my grandmother’s funeral last week. My five-year-old son asks where I am every day. And my wife will give birth, God willing, in March – and I don’t know if I will be by her side.”
“[All] because I have spoken my mind, and I had a lot more money than others who have spoken their mind, in my country. And that’s all it amounts to.”

articles.title: JV Ejercito: Projects lacking required documents to be removed
articles.summary: Senate Finance Committee chair Sen. JV Ejercito on Saturday said he would not allow projects without a program of works and other required documents to be included in the proposed national budget.

blocks.text: PROPOSED 2027 NAT'L BUDGET
Published November 14, 2026 10:44pm
Senate Finance Committee chair Sen. JV Ejercito on Saturday said he would not allow projects without a program of works and other required documents to be included in the proposed national budget.
The House-approved General Appropriations Bill (GAB) has drawn criticism over alleged budget insertions amounting to more than P1 trillion.

“Hindi na tayo papayag sa mga proyekto na walang Program of Works, walang Certificate of Implementability, walang Regional Development Council approval, at walang geotagging, lalo na sa mga infrastructure projects,” Ejercito said in a radio program.
(We will no longer allow projects without a Program of Works, Certificate of Implementability, Regional Development Council approval, and geotagging, especially infrastructure projects.)
Ejercito said his team was reviewing 6,271 infrastructure projects in the GAB to check whether they complied with these requirements.
“Nililinya natin ngayon ang bawat entry, ang bawat proyekto. Talagang napakahirap kasi kailangan mong tingnan at busisiin ang bawat isa,” he said.
(We are going through every entry and every project. It is really difficult because each one needs to be examined and scrutinized.)

The senator also met with Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Secretary Giovanni Lopez and his predecessor, former DPWH chief and now Transportation Secretary Vince Dizon, to remove projects that lacked the necessary documents.
The DPWH had been given until November 3 to submit the documents justifying the additional projects. Those that failed to meet the requirements would be removed, Ejercito said.
He stressed the need to prioritize flagship infrastructure projects over regional projects.

Ejercito said major projects such as the North-South Commuter Railway, Metro Manila Subway Project, Bataan-Cavite Interlink Bridge and Laguna Lakeshore Road Network Project could generate jobs and attract investments in the long run.

He said he was aiming to finish the committee report by November 20, with plenary deliberations scheduled to begin on November 23. Plenary debates are expected to conclude by December 1.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Napping Kansas driver whose truck sped on to soccer field and killed two won’t be charged
articles.summary:
Authorities declined to file charges against napping woman whose truck accelerated on to field during youth game

A soccer mom napping in her pickup truck when it suddenly accelerated on to…

blocks.text: A soccer mom napping in her pickup truck when it suddenly accelerated on to the field at a Kansas youth tournament where her child was playing, killing two people, won’t face criminal charges, a prosecutor has said.

Investigators believe the 34-year-old woman had failed to put the Chevrolet 1500 in park and likely put her foot on the gas pedal while sleeping at the Stryker Sports Complex in Wichita on 17 October. They conducted multiple interviews and even ran a test in the same parking spot with a similar vehicle.
“I cannot prove she consciously disregarded a tremendous risk to people on that field,” the Sedgwick county district attorney, Marc Bennett, said on Thursday.

He acknowledged the public might find his decision strange. Bennett’s 28-page report listed possible crimes that might be triggered when a person causes the death of another person but said none fit the soccer field tragedy under Kansas law.
“If I could charge somebody, why wouldn’t I?” Bennett said at a news conference. “But I also have an obligation to stand up and say, ‘It’s not here.’”

The two people killed at the scene were Cole Adrian, six, and Nicholas Schafer, 35, both from McPherson, Kansas, police said. Ten others ranging in age from five to 68 were reported injured and treated at area hospitals.
The Wichita police chief, Joe Sullivan, said his department spoke to victims and families before the report and other information were released publicly.

“Every lead was examined. Every piece of evidence was reviewed. Every reasonable avenue available to us was pursued … Our responsibility is not to fill gaps with assumptions or speculation,” Sullivan said.
The report said the day started with the woman driving to the soccer field with three children. After two games, they left the Stryker complex for a meal and returned by 2.30pm for another game.

While one child went to a field to play, the mom and her two other children remained in the pickup truck. She said she was going to take a nap, and a daughter covered the windshield with a two-panel sunscreen, the report said. Less than an hour later, the vehicle began to move.
“There is no evidence to support the conclusion that she knew the truck was still in drive, or evidence to explain what motive she would have had to do so,” the report said.

Wichita police detectives ran an identical test. They parked a Chevy 1500 in the same stall and also in drive mode – and “the truck stayed in place until the accelerator was pressed,” the report said.
“We sat there and waited and waited,” Bennett said at a news conference. “After about 15 minutes we went, ‘This truck isn’t moving.’ … Tires against a 7in curb and it did not move.”
Investigators said they interviewed more than 30 witnesses. Blood tests showed no evidence of drugs that would have impaired the driver’s judgment, the report said.
The report said the woman awoke to screams inside and outside the truck and the feeling of the vehicle moving.
Bennett said people who immediately pulled the driver from the truck found her sleepy, “sobbing, at turns described as frantic, hysterical, saying, ‘I’m sorry, I’m sorry. What have I done?’”
According to Bennett, the case could be tried in civil court.
Guardian staff contributed reporting

articles.title: Marcos signs EO adopting AI framework, creates national council
articles.summary: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has signed an executive order adopting the Artificial Intelligence (AI) Governance Framework and creating the National Artificial Intelligence Council.

blocks.text: Published November 14, 2026 10:30pm

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has signed an executive order adopting the country's Artificial Intelligence (AI) Governance Framework and creating the National Artificial Intelligence Council (NAIC) to oversee its implementation.

Signed on November 12, Executive Order No. 131 adopts the AI Governance Framework as the national strategic guide for policy formulation, regulatory coordination, institutional development, capacity-building and other governance measures necessary to support and strengthen the Philippine AI ecosystem.

The framework builds on the National AI Strategy for the Philippines, which was approved in May 2025, and had earlier been approved by the National Innovation Council as the national policy framework for responsible AI development, deployment and use.
During a press briefing on Saturday, Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro said the executive order recognizes AI as a tool that can help improve the lives of Filipinos.
"Kailangan tiyakin din na ang pag-unlad ng AI ay may konkretong pakinabang sa mga manggagawa, negosyo, komunidad at buong bansa," Castro said.
(We also need to ensure that advances in AI bring concrete benefits to workers, businesses, communities and the entire country.)
"Layon nitong tiyakin na ang AI ay maipatutupad nang responsable, ligtas, etikal at may sapat na proteksyon upang mapanatili ang tiwala ng publiko," she added.
(The measure aims to ensure that AI is implemented responsibly, safely and ethically, with adequate safeguards to maintain public trust.)— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Bomb found at Illinois ethanol plant, prompting evacuations
articles.summary:
Peoria officials said a bomb was found at BioUrja Renewables and later defused; FBI said it is investigating

Residents were ordered to evacuate parts of an

blocks.text: Residents were ordered to evacuate parts of an Illinois community on Friday after the mayor there said authorities found a bomb at a local ethanol- and alcohol-production plant.

The discovery reported at BioUrja Renewables in Peoria triggered a mandatory evacuation over a one-mile evacuation zone encompassing sections of that city as well as the adjacent municipality of East Peoria.
“It is real – this is a real thing,” Peoria’s mayor, Rita Ali, said, according to local news outlet WMBD. “We know that is a real threat. We know it is a bomb.”
Peoria’s police chief, Brad Dixon, said at a news conference early on Saturday that bomb technicians had rendered the object in question safe.
But Dixon asked for the public’s patience as investigators searched BioUrja Renewals’ expansive facility for other explosive devices, as the Peoria news outlet WEEK reported.
“We don’t know if there are other devices,” Ali remarked.

Meanwhile, Ryan Presley of the FBI, who is in charge of the bureau’s field office about an hour away in Springfield, Illinois, said agents would pursue whoever was responsible “tirelessly” and “bring them to justice”.

At about 7.05pm local time on Friday, the Peoria police department had announced that officers were “actively investigating a reported bomb threat at BioUrja Renewables”. The agency then urged “anyone who lives or works within a one-mile radius of the facility to immediately evacuate their homes and businesses until further notice”.

The police’s statement said the evacuation notice had been “issued out of an abundance of caution while officers and emergency personnel investigate the threat”, which officials initially referred to as a suspicious package. The city offered the Manual Academy school as a temporary shelter, and police said anyone who needed assistance evacuating their home or business could call for help.

In a separate statement, the municipal government of neighboring East Peoria acknowledged that the evacuation zone associated with the package at BioUrja Renewables extended into part of that city. The East Peoria government said it expected to provide an update at about 9am local time on Saturday, but in the meantime all evacuations would remain in place.
“This is not a hoax,” the Illinois state senator Dave Koehler said during the early Saturday news conference. “This has gone beyond that … This is serious. This is serious.”

Friday’s BioUrja Renewables case came amid a particularly chaotic day in the US marked by a nationwide Federal Aviation Administration-ordered nationwide ground stop at US airports that was in effect for about four hours, canceling or delaying more than 11,000 US flights.

The country’s nerves were also frayed by a tanker which struck a cruise ship docked on the Mississippi River in New Orleans on Friday afternoon. First responders had to rescue passengers from the river’s water after the cruise ship turned on its side, and there were more than 30 injuries reported. But none of those injuries were critical, and there were no fatalities reported in association with the crash.

articles.title: DFA: 80% of South China Sea Code of Conduct completed, salient issues remain
articles.summary: Southeast Asian nations and China have completed negotiations on 80% of the proposed Code of Conduct (COC) on the South China Sea ahead of next week's ASEAN Summit in Manila, the Department of…

blocks.text: Published November 14, 2026 10:11pm

Southeast Asian nations and China have completed negotiations on 80% of the proposed Code of Conduct (COC) on the South China Sea ahead of next week's ASEAN Summit in Manila, the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) said Saturday.
At a news conference in Pasay City, DFA Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro said significant progress had been made in the COC negotiations under the Philippines' ASEAN chairship.

"Since our chairship, a lot has been, the progress of the Code of Conduct is really hastened and there might just be a definitive possibility, but definitely a statement will be released," Lazaro said.

"Let's give it a little bit more time, as this is still subject of discussions. But I just want to say, at this point of time, 80% of the paragraphs, the paper itself, the document itself is finished. So, there will be just some salient points," she added.

The proposed code seeks to establish rules to prevent disputes in the South China Sea from spiraling out of control and developing into a major armed conflict that could involve the United States, a Philippine ally, and other countries in the region.

Lazaro earlier said ASEAN and China want to avoid a situation in the South China Sea similar to that in the Strait of Hormuz, which has prompted both sides to pursue negotiations on a Code of Conduct.
Malacañang, meanwhile, said it remains hopeful that the COC will be signed before the Philippines' ASEAN chairmanship ends.
"Bawat araw dapat may pag-asa (Every day should bring hope)," Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro said.

"Sa ngayon, hindi rin natin masasabi kung talagang hindi ito magkakaroon ng konklusyon sa 49th ASEAN Summit dahil ang gusto pa rin ng Pangulo ay masapinal sa panahon na ang Pilipinas ang ASEAN chair," she added.
(At this point, we cannot say for certain that the issue will not be resolved during the 49th ASEAN Summit, as the President still wants it finalized while the Philippines holds the ASEAN chairship.)

Four ASEAN member states—Malaysia, the Philippines, Vietnam, and Brunei—are involved in the long-standing territorial disputes in the South China Sea, an important passageway for global trade and commerce. The other two claimants are China and Taiwan.

In August 2018, ASEAN and China agreed on a single draft of the COC. In November 2018, both sides agreed to finalize the document within three years, beginning in 2019. However, no final agreement has been reached since then. —VBL, GMA News

articles.title: Vancouver duo's song goes viral after featuring in Grand Theft Auto VI
articles.summary: Bob Moses didn’t have to steal a car, pull off a heist, or even pick up a controller to score big with Grand Theft Auto VI. All the Vancouver-based electronic duo needed was a killer song and an…

image.caption: Vancouver-based electronic music duo Bob Moses have a song featured in Grand Theft Auto VI. (Hunter Monero/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: British Columbia

Bob Moses didn’t have to steal a car, pull off a heist, or even pick up a controller to score big with Grand Theft Auto VI. All the Vancouver-based electronic duo needed was a killer song and an email from Rockstar Games.
Bob Moses says Inner Light has racked up 50 million more streams since being featured in GTA trailer
· The Canadian Press
· Posted: Nov 14, 2026 9:00 AM EST | Last Updated: 31 minutes ago
Bob Moses didn’t have to steal a car, pull off a heist, or even pick up a controller to score big with Grand Theft Auto VI.
All the Canadian electronic duo needed was a killer song and an email from Rockstar Games.

They say their 2021 collaboration with British musician Elderbrook, Inner Light, has racked up more than 50 million additional streams since being featured in an extended trailer for the game in late August.

Fans have waited more than a decade for GTA VI, which finally arrives Thursday. But Inner Light has already taken on a life of its own, spreading across social media and reaching listeners far beyond the electronic music scene.

items: Is Grand Theft Auto VI the most anticipated video game of all time? Here are some reasons why

blocks.text: Vancouver's Tom Howie and Jimmy Vallance, who formed the Grammy-nominated duo in 2012, say their manager emailed them earlier this year with a request from Rockstar to use their song, with few details about how it would be featured.
"We were like, sweet, GTA is a big game. And then we sort of forgot about it," recalls Howie.
Months later, their phones lit up with messages from people they hadn't heard from in years.
It turned out Inner Light had landed a prime spot during the trailer’s climax, its haunting, synth-driven melodies underscoring an emotional speech about living in one’s "glory days."
"It became the part that everyone clipped and re-shared and kind of made the song go viral," says Vallance.
Spotify says the track saw a 500 per cent surge in streams since the trailer dropped, with daily additions to listeners’ playlists increasing by more than 3,000 per cent.
The unexpected success comes as musicians face mounting pressure to create viral moments in an increasingly crowded streaming landscape.
Jimmy Vallance, left, and Tom Howie of the Vancouver-based electronic music duo Bob Moses. (Hunter Monero/The Canadian Press)
Vallance says the experience reinforced something the duo has learned over years of navigating an industry reshaped by TikTok and social media: there's no reliable formula for a hit.
"You can't engineer this in a lab," he says.
"Someone somewhere liked a song that we wrote one day and put it in the trailer, and then that connected with millions of people."
The duo says they were paid a relatively modest licensing fee.
"I forget how much money it was, but it's not enough to remember," says Howie.
"The opportunity is definitely in the potential for the reach, not in the paycheque."

items: New Wolverine video game features Squamish Nation's language, B.C. locations

blocks.text: Toronto music supervisor Heather Gardner says that's not unusual.
Gardner, president of the Guild of Music Supervisors Canada, says a placement in a gaming behemoth like GTA can be valuable even when the licensing payment itself isn't especially lucrative.
"It's such a cultural icon," she says of the franchise.

"No one can pay their bills in exposure, but it really is in an industry that is so saturated musically right now. Everybody is looking for a way to break through and to get eyes and ears on them and a sync, beyond the payment, is absolutely that."
Music integral to GTA

Music has long been integral to the GTA experience, with the franchise’s fictional radio stations introducing generations of players to an eclectic mix of genres as they cruise city streets, mow down pedestrians and outrun police.
For GTA VI, Grammy-winning French electronic duo Justice composed the score, while Rockstar plans to release an album of original songs Thursday, featuring SZA, Tame Impala and Keith Richards.
The musical celebrations will continue into the weekend with a GTA-themed concert in Miami featuring Travis Scott and Cardi B.
Gardner says video games offer a particularly powerful form of music discovery because players aren't simply watching or listening.
"You're an active participant in the media in a way that no other form can do."
A still from the new Grand Theft Auto VI video game. (Rockstar Games/The Canadian Press)

Vallance is a longtime fan of the GTA series, recalling playing the original top-down game of the '90s on a friend's computer before becoming captivated by the leap to three-dimensional gameplay in Grand Theft Auto III.

But it was the 1980s-inspired soundtrack of Grand Theft Auto: Vice City that left the deepest musical impression, introducing him to acts such as A Flock of Seagulls and sparking an interest in the synth-pop sounds of that era.

Vallance says it's a "huge honour" his own music has now become part of the franchise's cultural orbit. The placement has also given the duo a moment of validation after years of navigating the uncertainties of a music career.
"Every once in a while something happens and you're like, 'Oh, we're a real band.'"

items: How this Vancouver developer turned a unicycling obsession into a video game

blocks.text: GTA VI is estimated to bring in $3.25 billion to $5.2 billion in first-week sales, according to market research firm Newszoo.
Howie believes the game serves as a tastemaker at a time when audiences are increasingly fragmented across countless entertainment platforms.
"There's not many things that tons of people do all together anymore. We used to all watch the same shows and listen to the same radio stations and read the same things," he says.
"GTA is one of the very few things that a lot of people still come around to; that's a unifying thing on a scale that doesn't really exist in today's age."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Alex Nino Gheciu is a reporter with The Canadian Press.

articles.title: Choking fires, deadly heat and devastating floods: 2026 in extreme weather
articles.summary:
People around the world have contended with unprecedented weather events and their fatal effects caused by the climate catastrophe

After the world’s hottest summer since records began in…
articles.byline: Jonathan Watts; graphics by Sara Fiorillo

blocks.text: After the world’s hottest summer since records began in 1850, the death toll from extreme weather in 2026 is already in the high tens of thousands. That is a conservative estimate and is certain to rise much higher.

As Cop31 continues and scientists warn that climate breakdown may be accelerating, the Guardian looks back at a year of droughts, fires and floods as a reminder that, unless the world takes urgent action to cut emissions, this disastrous year will be one of the best of the rest of our lives.
January Fourth-hottest January on record

blocks.caption: A fire in Longwood, a town in Victoria, Australia, in early January. Photograph: Michael Currie/AAP

blocks.text: Extreme heat fuels wildfires in Australia As temperatures jump nearly 20C (68F) above average, Victoria and other southern states register new heat records, including 50C in Port Augusta and the tiny opal mining town of Andamooka. Melbourne hospitals report a 25% increase in heat-related illnesses, while authorities in many areas struggle with wildfires. Scientists say the supercharged climate has made the heatwave five times more likely. Heatwaves already cause more deaths in Australia than all other natural hazards combined.
February Fourth-hottest February on record

blocks.caption: People clear mud and debris outside homes in the aftermath of a storm, in Juiz de Fora, Brazil. Photograph: Andre Coelho/EPA

blocks.text: Mudslides kill 72 in Brazil after record rain The city of Juiz de Fora in Minas Gerais records its wettest ever month, triggering landslides that sweep away hundreds of homes in poor communities on unstable hillsides. Floods also disrupt Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo. More than 10,000 people are displaced.
March Fourth-hottest March on record

blocks.caption: Motorists drive through heavy rains in the Kibera slums in Nairobi, Kenya.   Photograph: Donwilson Odhiambo/Getty Images

blocks.text: Devastating floods across much of the world In Ethiopia, at least 131 people are killed in floods and mudslides that bury entire villages. Eighty die in Kenya and 18 in Tanzania. The Arabian peninsula is battered by fierce winds and heavy downpours that flood the streets of the desert kingdom. Hailstones the size of tennis balls fall in Oman and lightning storms leave cities in the UAE inundated with water. Many areas report record rainfall. At least 30 die in Afghanistan as heavy rains trigger landslides. Hong Kong is soaked in twice the usual monthly precipitation. Flood waters in southern Russia submerge homes and leave more than 300,000 without electricity. Huge tracts of farmland are left underwater in Argentina and Chile.

World’s energy imbalance accelerates rapidly The World Meteorological Organization reveals an alarming buildup of energy in Earth’s system. More than 90% is stored in the oceans, where warming has more than doubled over the past two decades compared with the average over the previous 45 years. This makes weather more extreme and threatens health and food supplies. António Guterres, the UN secretary general, says: “The global climate is in a state of emergency. Planet Earth is being pushed beyond its limits. Every key climate indicator is flashing red.” Guterres urges the world to cut fossil fuel emissions as rapidly as possible to minimise future risks. However, CO2 in the atmosphere continues to rise.
April Second-hottest April on record

blocks.caption: A utility pole blocks a road in Saipan after a super typhoon with ferocious winds and relentless rains shredded tin roofs and forced people to take cover from flying tree limbs. Photograph: AP

blocks.text: Super typhoon tears through Micronesia, Guam and Saipan At peak intensity on 12 April, Sinlaku registers a wind speed of 295km/h (183mph) – roughly the same as a Shinkansen bullet train and the joint highest recorded by a storm in the western Pacific basin so early in the year. It is also the deadliest in decades, killing 12, leaving 43,000 without power, forcing mass evacuation and causing $1.5bn (£1.1bn) in damages. This will remain one of the most powerful storms of 2026, superseded only by Super Typhoon Champi that will strike Taiwan and Japan in October.
May Second-hottest May on record

blocks.caption: A man seeks relief from the heat as temperatures rise in New Delhi, India. Photograph: Rajat Gupta/EPA

blocks.text: Hundreds of millions endure deadly heat in south Asia At least 47 heat-related deaths are reported in southern Asia as temperatures soar above 45C in several Indian and Bangladeshi cities, and hit a peak of 52C in Pakistan’s southern province of Sindh. Scientists warn that the climate crisis is exposing hundreds of millions of people in south Asia to longer, deadlier pre-monsoon heat.
June Second-hottest June on record

blocks.caption: People assess the aftermath of landslides and flooding next to houses damaged in Attécoubé, a suburb of Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire. Photograph: Chris Boli/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Ocean heat enters uncharted territory Sea surface temperature graphs begin to jag upwards and away from all previous highs on 21 June, starting a trend that will worsen over the rest of the year. This alarms scientists because oceans absorb more than 90% of the excess energy in Earth’s system. If the seas start to release that heat then the land and air will get warmer more quickly. This coincides with the emergence of the latest El Niño, which is confirmed on 2 June.

Arctic and Antarctic swelter in unprecedented warmth Instead of the usual winter snow and ice, scientists at the Esperanza base on the Trinity peninsula of Antarctica are astonished to see rain and dirt outside their windows after an eight-day heatwave that peaked with a record temperature of 15C on 6 June. At the other end of the planet, the Arctic experiences its warmest ever June. Beliy Island, Siberia, registers 28.3C on 25 June, the highest temperature ever recorded that far north in the Eurasian Arctic.

West African deluge takes heavy toll Relentless rains claim almost 100 lives in west Africa from May to June. Record downpours of up to 140mm (5.5in) in a single day are made five times more likely and 23% more intense by the human-caused climate crisis. Floods and mudslides kill 59 in Côte d’Ivoire, 35 in Ghana and five in Togo.
after newsletter promotion
July Joint-hottest July on record

Fires choke Canada and Europe Almost 1,000 wildfires sweep across Canada, charring 3m hectares (7.4m acres) and sending a haze of smoke as far as New York. On 15 July Toronto registers the world’s worst air quality as a result of the haze. Smoke kills 4,000 people in Canada each year, almost four times as many as at the start of the century. Meanwhile, in Europe, prolonged droughts create tinderbox conditions for wildfires in Greece, Portugal, Italy, Norway, Germany, Spain and France. They burn 686,000 hectares in Europe, twice the average of the past 20 years.

Extreme weather disrupts US 250th birthday festivities and the World Cup Half of the US population is under a heat alert before 4 July independence celebrations, disrupting Donald Trump’s Great American State Fair on the National Mall in Washington and other events. Dozens of heat-related deaths are reported and thousands experience power cuts.
At least nine World Cup games are played in potentially dangerous heat and humidity, while fierce storms delay three matches by more than an hour, including Mexico v England.
August Hottest August on record

Nepal glacier collapse kills at least 1,300 Lhende Khola river valley communities are swept away after a 2 sq km (0.8 sq miles) slab of rock and glacier ice falls 1,400 metres (4,600ft) in the Himalayas, triggering a flood of water and debris. More than 5,000 people are missing and 8,600 need medical attention. Scientists say unusually warm temperatures and long-term permafrost degradation owing to the climate crisis were among the likely causes of the catastrophe.

Europe’s murderous heat forces reactor shutdown The UK and France are among a host of nations that swelter through the warmest summer (June to August) in European history. The heat kills an estimated 50,000 people in cities across the continent. Two-thirds of those excess deaths are attributable to the climate crisis. Many more are likely to have died in rural areas. As droughts spread, Romania is forced to shut down its only nuclear power station because the cooling system could not be replenished by low water levels in the Danube River.
September Second-hottest September on record

Record heat and deadly storms lash Asia Hundreds are killed and millions evacuated as the world’s most populous continent experiences its hottest September and severe storms. Typhoon Dujuan kills at least 10 people in Japan, with violent winds of 144km/h and 832mm of rain in only 48 hours on the island of Izu Oshima. Three die in a mudslide in eastern China during Typhoon Saudel. At least 102 are killed in India and Nepal amid rain that is nine times the norm in some places. Eight die and half a million are affected by flooding in Bangkok, Thailand.
October Hottest October on record

blocks.caption: Protesters clash with police officers in Jakarta, Indonesia, during a demonstration against President Prabowo Subianto’s handling of forest fires. Photograph: Willy Kurniawan/Reuters

blocks.text: Governments warned to brace for peak El Niño The UN disaster relief agency urges countries to prepare for an unprecedented “wrecking ball” El Niño that is forecast to peak around the end of the year. UK authorities advise households to stockpile a few days of basic supplies. Climate scientists project more than 450,000 people globally will die by February as a result of the additional heat brought by the super El Niño.

Protests in Indonesia after deadly fires Demonstrators in Jakarta protest against Indonesia’s worst fire season in a decade, which has scorched almost 2m hectares of forest – more than twice as big an area as last year. The choking haze is estimated to have killed 3,560 people in one month alone.

Roads turn to rivers in Chile After the heaviest October rainfall in 76 years, the Chilean government declares the Santiago district of Las Condes a “disaster zone”, with more than 1,000 people evacuated from their homes, some by helicopter.

Drought and fire in the Amazon rainforest Months of drought leave some of the world’s mightiest rivers, including the Rio Negro, Madeira and Tapajós, close to record low levels, curtailing the water transport of essential goods. This coincides with a sharp rise in fire activity in the central and eastern Amazon region, releasing so much smoke that the city of Manaus registers the second-worst air quality in the world on 12 October.
November

blocks.caption: Global fossil fuel emissions are likely to fall this year thanks to a shift away from oil and gas owing to high prices after the US-Israeli attack on Iran, and ever cheaper renewable alternatives. Photograph: Jesús Vargas/Getty Images

blocks.text: 2026 is forecast to be one of the hottest years in history

Global temperatures tie an all-time record of 2.04C above preindustrial levels, which was set in 2023. This year is forecast to be one of the four warmest years in history, along with 2023, 2024 and 2025. Sea surface temperatures are so high that the climate scientist Eliot Jacobson calculates the odds of being this far above the norm at 33tn to one. Meanwhile, the amount of CO2 in the atmosphere reaches a peak not seen in 2m years. On the plus side, global fossil fuel emissions are likely to fall this year thanks to a shift away from oil and gas owing to high prices after the US-Israeli attack on Iran, and ever cheaper renewable alternatives.

articles.title: Philippines to host ASEAN Maritime Center - DFA
articles.summary: The ASEAN Maritime Center is set to be established in the Philippines, the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) announced on Saturday.

blocks.text: Published November 14, 2026 8:49pm
The ASEAN Maritime Center is set to be established in the Philippines, the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) announced on Saturday.
DFA Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro made the announcement during a press briefing at the International Media Center in Pasay City.
"During the foreign ministers' meeting, we adopted the concept note. The terms of reference of the ASEAN Maritime Center will be based in the Philippines," Lazaro said.
"We haven't really decided all the other issues concerning this, but this is a very important result of our chairship," she added.
Lazaro said the center will serve as a knowledge hub and support platform for maritime-related initiatives and issues, in line with the priorities identified by ASEAN member states.
"It involves issues on port authorities. It involves the whole gamut of the blue economy," she said.
In a previous statement, Lazaro underscored the need to strengthen maritime security and cooperation among ASEAN member states. —VBL, GMA News

Brunei Sultan Haji Hassanal Bolkiah and United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres arrived in the Philippines on Saturday, ahead of the opening ceremony of the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits on Sunday.
Bolkiah was accompanied by his son, Prince Abdul Mateen, who currently serves as the foreign minister of the oil-rich country.
Guterres is also expected to hold a bilateral meeting with ASEAN Chairperson and President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on the sidelines of the summit.
Earlier on Saturday, several other leaders arrived in the Philippines, including those from Timor-Leste, Australia, Canada, Brazil, the Lao People’s Democratic Republic, and Vietnam.
The 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits will run from November 15 to 17.
The meetings will be held at the Philippine International Convention Center (PICC) in Pasay City. —VBL, GMA News

articles.title: Ukraine: Zelenskyy says security deal could go to referendum
articles.summary: The US has broached the idea of Kyiv giving up the Donbas region in exchange for NATO membership, the Ukrainian president said.

image.caption: Zelenskyy said he could put any comprehensive security deal to a public voteImage: Francisco Seco/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said US peace envoys asked whether Kyiv would withdraw from its eastern region of ‌Donbas ⁠in exchange ⁠for joining NATO, according to remarks to the media published on Saturday.
The suggestion was made following the latest round of peace talks in Abu Dhabi to bring Russia's nearly 5-year war in Ukraine to a close.
What did Zelenskyy say?
The Ukrainian leader told reporters: "The Americans raised a question: 'What if Ukraine joins NATO? Would ⁠Ukraine ​withdraw from Donbas?'"

Zelenskyy repeated Kyiv's position that it was not willing to cede territory to Russia. But he added that if the country reached a comprehensive deal, including security guarantees, a ‌strong ​and well-funded Ukrainian army and funds to rebuild, he would put the question ​to the public in a referendum.
"That ​is why ⁠I believe NATO is back on the ⁠agenda. ​But you have also heard [Russian President Vladimir] Putin's signals, and this is an extremely difficult conversation."
Zelenskyy said the prospect of NATO membership in exchange for withdrawing from Donbas has not been raised before.
He also warned about Moscow's plan to change the continent's security architecture, saying it could lead to more conflict.
Putin has demanded that NATO pull back its troops from the Russian border, which European Union leaders have strongly criticized.
"This is dangerous because, in my view, it is precisely things like this that lead to wars or escalations," Zelenskyy added.
"Real security in Europe means the EU and NATO. That's it. There is no other security in Europe."
Europe chooses representatives for Ukraine peace talks
Europe to play bigger role in peace talks
On Friday, the EU said several European diplomats would take part in future Ukraine peace talks, including Germany, France, the United Kingdom and Poland.
Moscow has long insisted that European states be excluded from the negotiations because they support Ukraine.
Russian forces strike Zaporizhzhia
The comments come as Russia’s Defence Ministry said its ⁠forces ⁠had captured the ​settlement of Tersianka in ​Ukraine’s southeastern ​Zaporizhzhia ‌region, news agency Interfax reported.

Interfax cited the ministry as saying that Russian ​forces had struck Ukrainian energy and ​transport infrastructure used by ⁠the ​military, along with ammunition ​depots and ​drone production ‌and storage sites.
Russia has targeted power stations across Ukraine in waves of ballistic and cruise missile attacks, cutting power and heating to millions of people as temperatures plunge.
Zelenskyy warned that Putin was "betting everything" on this winter's war campaign, which Kyiv insists is aimed at hurting public morale.

articles.title: New facilities in Laos and Cambodia: Is China expanding its military presence in Southeast Asia?
articles.summary: China has been growing its economic relationships in Southeast Asia. Now new military facilities in Laos and Cambodia are causing smaller countries to worry China's military networks are also…

image.caption: A Chinese soldier during joint maneuvers with Cambodia in May 2024Image: Heng Sinith/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: It's often said that maintaining good relations with your neighbors is essential. So in early November, China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi invited his counterparts from Laos, Cambodia, Vietnam, Thailand and Myanmar to Beijing.
There the six countries agreed on closer economic and security cooperation.
The visit is just one example of China's growing influence on Southeast Asia. It's not just about trade or infrastructure either, it's also increasingly about military cooperation.
New airbase in Laos

For instance, at the end of September, China and Laos opened a joint military support and training center north of the Laotian capital, Vientiane. Initially Laotian air force pilots are to be trained at the Ban Keun airfield, China has said.

Earlier in 2025 China expanded its footprint at Cambodia's Ream naval base. China uses the facility on the Gulf of Thailand for logistics and training. And while Japanese and Vietnamese ships can visit the port, they're docked at a southern quay and it's unclear if other navies can use the same facilities under the same conditions as China.
"It remains to be seen how this [Ban Keun] will change China's military access to Southeast Asia," says Marco Bünte, a professor of Asian politics at the University Erlangen Nuremberg in Germany.

blocks.caption: A satellite image shows construction of Ban Keun airfield in LaosImage: Vantor/REUTERS

blocks.text: In recent years, China has significantly expanded its economic influence in the region.
The China-Laos railway and other infrastructure projects connect Laos more closely with its northern neighbor. Laos is also heavily indebted to China.
Bünte points out that Laos and Cambodia have been close military partners of China for some time and the new facility in Laos can be seen as another step towards deepening cooperation.
If that proves correct, "China would gain strategic depth in mainland Southeast Asia," Bünte explained. "It would also give China better military access to the South China Sea."

Johann Fuhrmann, head of the Konrad Adenauer Foundation's Beijing office, points out that one should distinguish between training Laotian pilots and any potential use of the facilities by Chinese armed forces later.
"China gains influence when it co-designs the training and operation of such facilities over several years," Fuhrmann told DW.
Laos: A country in the grip of the Chinese?
Chinese planes in Laos

But nobody should underestimate China's military positioning, Bünte continued. "China is expanding its military operational capabilities here although I wouldn't speak of military hegemony because China hasn't achieved that yet."

With regard to the Laotian airbase, China says that Laotian pilots will be trained there. But beside military transporters and helicopters, Laos actually only has three light combat aircraft by Russia's Yakovlev works.

According to the aviation media outlet FlightGlobal, four more K-8s, Chinese two-seat intermediate jet trainer and light attack aircrafts, are in service there. Satellite images analyzed by the Reuters news agency in early October show eight K-8s at the base — even thought this doesn't necessarily mean they are stationed there permanently.
Fuhrmann doesn't think anybody should jump to conclusions about this.
"The idea of ​​a Chinese air corridor is more of a future scenario than something that has already been proven," he says.
For example, the runway at Ban Keun is only 2,000 meters (6,562 feet) long, which makes it too short for large Chinese bombers. These usually require 3,000 meters.

blocks.caption: A 2022 satellite image shows the Ream naval base in CambodiaImage: picture alliance/AP

blocks.text: The crucial question is what rights China will be granted, Fuhrmann continues: "Will China have to obtain the approval of the respective government for every new use? Or are there longer-term commitments that both sides can invoke, even in times of crisis?"
Surrounding countries are reacting differently to what appears to be China's growing influence in Laos, Cambodia and Myanmar because these countries are already considered closer to China.

Other Southeast Asian nations are hedging, trying to expand their relationship with China without severing ties with the US and also maintaining economic links with other Western nations. China's involvement offers them additional options and Beijing wants to explore those possibilities. That's just pragmatic though, Bünte says of the smaller Asian nations.
"Overall, these states… try to keep as many options open as possible," he notes.
China's gray zone warfare in the Pacific
China: 'Not against third parties'

Vietnam and the Philippines are watching developments particularly closely. Both have territorial disputes with China in the South China Sea. But Vietnam also has close historical ties to Laos and trained its own military there.

In early November, the Vietnamese government declared that any military cooperation must serve peace and stability and referred to the Treaty of Amity and Cooperation in Southeast Asia, commonly known as the ASEAN Treaty. China is not an ASEAN member but has also stated that its activities are not directed against any third parties.
"So far, these are individual steps," Bünte adds. "We would have to wait and see if this leads to a broader military alliance in the years to come."
Fuhrmann says that Western nations should help strengthen the smaller countries in the region and take their interests seriously.
"Ultimately, a counterweight can only be achieved through tangible contributions, not through warnings or lectures from Europe," he says.
This story was originally published in German.

blocks.text: What you need to know

items: Solar energy output in Germany is drawing close a record total of more than 100 terawatt-hours in a single calendar year
Economics experts are warning that the country is living beyond its means
Health care cuts mean people might have to pay privately to avoid long waiting times, says the national association for statutory physicians
Experts in Germany have warned against too much reliance on a sole provider after a major outage at Microsoft affected German businesses

blocks.text: This is a roundup of the top stories from and about Germany on November 14, 2026:
November 14, 2026
Solar energy output set for record high in Germany in 2026

An above-average number of sunshine hours and the growing number of photovoltaic facilities has contributed to solar energy production that is approaching a record total for Germany, an industry association says.

By September 27, solar energy output had reached 90.2 terawatt-hours, which is already more than the 90 terawatt-hours generated for all of 2025, according to the German Solar Association (BSW -Solar) in Berlin.

That means that solar energy in net electricity generation in Germany is likely to reach a record level of more than 100 terawatt-hours in a single calendar year — almost 10 times the amount of electricity used by a major city like Hamburg in a year.
It is also almost 50 times as much as the 2.2 terawatt-hours generated byx solar power 20 years ago.
Carsten Körnig, the managing director of BSW-Solar, said the likely record was an important milestone as the world seeks to move away from climate-changing fossil fuels.
"Photovoltaics has developed from a niche technology into a cornerstone of our electricity supply," Körnig said.
"Society as a whole benefits from this: through cheaper electricity, fewer energy import and significantly lower climate-related damages," he said.
At 17.8% of total power generation, photovoltaics was the third most important energy source of domestically produced electricity behind wind power — the top energy source — followed by coal.

articles.title: Hungarian authorities uncover $20m during probe of Orbán-era minister
articles.summary: Prime Minister Péter Magyar promised a sweeping anti-corruption drive after ousting Orbán in April.

blocks.text: Nearly $20m (£14.8m) in cash has been found hidden in farm buildings and buried in forests as part of an investigation into a former minister of Viktor Orbán, authorities have said.

Miklós Seszták, who served as minister of national development for four of the ex-prime minister's 16-year rule, is accused of accepting bribes as part of a scheme involving the state transport company. He has denied any wrongdoing.
Hungary's new Prime Minister Péter Magyar unseated Orbán in a landslide election in April on the promise of launching a sweeping anti-corruption drive.
On Friday, following the two-day search for the cash - found in secluded locations across the country - Magyar described it as the end of the "mafia".

Investigators found wads of banknotes in safes, buried in woodlands and hidden in agricultural and residential buildings and warehouses, as part of the probe into Seszták, the National Asset Recovery and Protection Office (NVVH) said in a statement.
The cash amounted to "5,071,632,000 forints, €2,658,350 and $1,257,100", it added, bringing the combined value to $19.5m. It has been deposited into the Hungarian State Treasury, the body said.
The NVVH was established to investigate allegations of corruption during the Orbán rule, which Magyar has dubbed "Operation Purgatory".
Magyar promised Hungarians "regime change" during the election earlier this year and has set about undoing many Orbán-era policies since entering office.
Allegations of corruption and cronyism have long dogged Orbán, who during the course of his tenure turned Hungary into what the EU characterised as an "electoral autocracy".

articles.title: US has floated Ukraine ceding Donbas for Nato membership, Zelensky says
articles.summary: The Ukrainian president says US envoys touted the exchange as part of efforts to end the war with Russia.

blocks.text: US negotiators have touted the idea of Ukraine withdrawing its remaining forces from the eastern Donbas region in exchange for Nato membership, Volodymyr Zelensky has said.
The Ukrainian president's comments on Saturday come after US envoys visited Moscow and an EU summit in Dublin as part of ongoing efforts to end the war between Russia and Ukraine.
Kyiv has long sought membership of the military alliance as a condition of any peace deal to deter future threats, while Russia has said another Nato member on its border was unacceptable.
Zelensky has also consistently said Ukraine was unwilling to give up sovereign territory, despite Moscow's demands for it to cede the Donbas.
"The Americans raised a question: 'What if Ukraine joins Nato? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?' This was the first time this had been raised," Zelensky told reporters on Saturday.
He went on to say that if he received a proposal that contained security guarantees, no constraints on Ukraine's military and funds to rebuild the country, he would put it to a referendum.
US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff travelled to the Irish capital on Thursday to meet Zelensky, after a round of talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow the day prior.

Comments by both Putin and Kremlin officials suggest that Russia's position on the war has not shifted, and that Moscow's demands for territory and neutrality continue to far exceed what Ukraine is prepared to consider.
Moscow has previously proposed limits on the size of Ukraine's military, territorial concessions and Kyiv's guaranteed neutrality as conditions of a peace deal.
Ukraine has rejected these, arguing that such constraints would hamper its ability to stave off any future invasion.

There have, however, been recent signs the two can find common ground: last month, US First Lady Melania Trump was able to broker a temporary ceasefire in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky to allow for evacuations and aid deliveries.
US officials had previously said that Ukrainian Nato membership was off the table.
Zelensky said on Saturday that the US proposal made him believe that "Nato is back on the agenda".
But he cautioned: "You have also heard Putin's signals, and this is an extremely difficult conversation."
Russia currently occupies roughly a fifth of Ukrainian territory, including most of the Donetsk and Luhansk regions that compose the Donbas.

Ceding the small portions of land Ukraine still controls there would be a small concession in practical terms, but would be symbolically significant for Kyiv because it would constitute an acceptance of the Donbas being Russian.
Zelensky has previously spoken of retaking Russian-controlled territory in four of Ukraine's regions, as well as the Crimean peninsula, which Moscow annexed in 2014.

articles.title: Scam targeting minor hockey teams 'heartbreaking' for affected kids
articles.summary: Valerie Favreau, the chair of the Oromocto Minor Hockey Association, said two under-13 teams signed up for a tournament in Stanley, with each team losing around $750 in fake registration fees. It's a…

image.caption: The scam has also targeted minor hockey teams in other provinces. The head of Hockey New Brunswick said people should cross-reference the sign-up emails they are receiving with the official sanctioned list of tournaments. (Peter Evans/CBC)

blocks.text: New Brunswick

Valerie Favreau, the chair of the Oromocto Minor Hockey Association, said two under-13 teams signed up for a tournament in Stanley, with each team losing around $750 in fake registration fees. It's a type of scam that is referred to as "spear phishing," according to the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre.
RCMP says it is investigating reports of tournament scams
Valerie Favreau was "crushed" when she learned that two Oromocto minor hockey teams had been scammed by a new con that has made its way to New Brunswick.
"I was floored," she said. " I just couldn't believe it."
Favreau, the chair of the Oromocto Minor Hockey Association, said the association will often receive tournament sign-up information, which she will then forward to Oromocto teams.
But this new scam comes in the form of an email mimicking these sign-up calls, often with convincing graphics and names of real people and real tournaments.

Favreau said two under-13 teams signed up for a tournament that was supposed to happen in Stanley, each team losing around $750 in fake registration fees. She said the teams only found out they had been scammed when the schedule came out for the tournament and they weren't on it.

Valerie Favreau, the chair of the Oromocto Minor Hockey Association, said two U13 teams signed up for a tournament that was supposed to happen in Stanley. Each team lost around $750 in fake registration fees. (Shane Fowler/CBC)
As a mom to five hockey players, Favreau said the scam makes her angry.
"Parents and kids have to fundraise for all that money, and it's a lot of money," she said.
"It's really heartbreaking for the kids to also be excited about going to a tournament and then have it cancelled because it's not real.
"Like, scams are wrong. Doing it against kids, I think it's really low."
Scammers trick N.B. minor hockey teams into sending them fees for tournaments
The scam is not only targeting New Brunswick teams. A Nova Scotia team also fell victim to the scam, and Hockey Alberta issued a warning as well.

Nobody with the New Brunswick RCMP was available for an interview, but Cpl. Luc Picard said in an email the RCMP were aware of reports involving tournament registration scams targeting minor hockey teams and associations.
"We can confirm that the RCMP did [receive] complaints from the public about this," Picard wrote. "As these investigations remain active, we are unable to provide further details at this time."
The statement said the RCMP encourages organizations and individuals to exercise caution before sending money or sharing sensitive information.
Anyone who thinks they have fallen victim to a scam should report it to local police, their financial institution and the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre, Picard said.

Jeff Horncastle, the client and communications outreach officer with the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre, said this type of scam is referred to as spear phishing — a targeted form of fraud where criminals impersonate a trusted individual to deceive people into sending money or information.
"In other words, they really do their research on their target before, and we have seen them target minor hockey associations, churches, businesses," he said.

"In the first nine months of 2026, the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre received reports of approximately $87 million in losses linked to spear phishing, and that was an increase from $68 million in all of 2025. So it is a type of fraud that has been increasing quite rapidly."
The sophistication of spear phishing is also increasing.

Three years ago, Horncastle said there may have been signs that an attempt was fraudulent just based on the email's appearance. But now, he said, fraudsters have tools to help them write their email so language barriers aren't a factor and they have tools to help them research their target.

Horncastle said scammers can often create an email domain with one letter changed — like swapping a lowercase L for an uppercase I — or they can spoof an address so the real one doesn't show unless a person hovers over it.
"Technology and sophistication play a huge role in this type of fraud."

Nic Jansen, the executive director of Hockey New Brunswick, said his organization first heard about the scam about a month ago when it started appearing in Nova Scotia and Alberta, so he sent a memo to members.
Jansen said tournaments can cost upwards of $1,000.
Nic Jansen, executive director of Hockey New Brunswick, said the demand for tournaments can make it difficult for people to decipher between what is real and what is fake. (Submitted by Nic Jansen)
And he said a lot of New Brunswick tournaments sell out quickly. He hears concerns every season about the difficulty of getting into tournaments.
"There's tournaments that, like once posted, sell out almost instantly," Jansen said.
"There's certainly a willingness and a desire for teams to attend tournaments. … It's often the highlight of players' minor hockey season to go to these tournaments.
"I would say that the demand and the interest to attend tournaments makes it challenging to decipher between what's actually legitimate and what can be a scam."

Jansen said when a team gets an email, they should look at the sanctioned tournament list on Hockey New Brunswick's website and contact the host association directly if they have concerns about an email being real.

Favreau said she now gets tournament scam emails daily. But ever since two Oromocto teams were scammed, she now double and triple checks the sanctioned list from Hockey New Brunswick when she gets an email.
"I'm really doubting about everything right now," she said. "I'm really looking for signs. I'm really looking to make sure everything is legit."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Hannah Rudderham is a reporter with CBC New Brunswick. She grew up in Cape Breton, N.S., and moved to Fredericton in 2018. You can send story tips to hannah.rudderham@cbc.ca.

articles.title: Wolf Biermann at 90: The singer who defied East Germany
articles.summary: His life is a reflection of contemporary German history, which Biermann has addressed via his songs and sharp wit. Turning 90, he’s as feisty as ever.

image.caption: Wolf Biermann's powerful lyrics have caused political tremors — big and small — for decadesImage: Marcus Brandt/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: He mocks Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin as "political lovers," denounces the "endless fratricidal war by the River Jordan," and repeatedly invokes "Lady Liberty." It is a celebration of the freedom he once so painfully lacked in the former East Germany, and of the freedom people around the world still yearn for.

These themes run throughout Wolf Biermann's new album "Unterm Haar nur Himmel" ("Beneath Hair, Only Sky") released to mark his 90th birthday. The album's title is a characteristically poetic phrase coined by Biermann himself. It evokes the idea that however restrictive the world may become, the human mind and spirit remain free. Beneath the hair lies open sky: a metaphor for inner freedom, independence and imagination.

Biermann remains one of Germany's most influential singer-songwriters, and at 90, he shows little sign of putting down his guitar. Often described as Germany's answer to Bob Dylan, the outspoken troubadour continues to weigh in on the issues shaping the world today.

In his recent song "Moritat von den Liebespaaren" ("Ballad of the Lovers"), he delivers a simple but urgent message: no single person can save the world, yet everyone can help make it a better place. Above all, the song is a call to take responsibility for one's own life rather than remain a bystander.

blocks.caption: 'Operation Gomorrah' reduced Hamburg to rubble in 1943 and Wolf Biermann grew up — just like these children — amid the ruinsImage: dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: A child caught in the Allied firestorm

This outspokenness was instilled in Biermann early on. When he was born in Hamburg in 1936, Adolf Hitler was already in power. His father was a dockworker, a committed communist, a resistance fighter against the Nazis — and Jewish. Wolf was just three months old when the Gestapo, Hitler's secret police, arrested his father. He initially served time in prison before he was murdered by the Nazis at Auschwitz in early 1943.

Just a few months later, British and American bombers attacked Hamburg, unleashing a devastating firestorm. "Nothing in my life has shaped me more," Biermann has repeatedly said in interviews. When the air raid sirens sounded, his mother took him into an air raid shelter. The house above them was burning.

Yet Biermann says his memories of that time are rooted in a profound sense of trust in life. In an interview with the German magazine Chrismon, he recalled: "I pressed my face into my mother's soft coat so I could breathe. A sense of security in the midst of the end of the world. We stumbled out over the neighboring house and into the open. The firestorm lifted a burning roof into the air. Roaring corrugated metal, smoke everywhere. We searched for a way out. (...) Death was everywhere. 40,000 people died. They had no chance. But I did. My strong mama."
Avenging his father

His mother instilled communist and anti-fascist ideas in him with almost religious fervor. "My mother had only one goal after those dark years," Biermann recalls. "I was supposed to survive so that I could, as she put it rather grandly, one day take revenge for my father's death. I was supposed to build communism."

In 1953, while countless people were fleeing from East Germany, Biermann moved there of his own free will — after all, communism was the official state ideology. He was just 16 at the time. In East Berlin, he studied political economy, mathematics and philosophy. His role models were writers Bertolt Brecht and Heinrich Heine. He began working as an assistant director at the Berliner Ensemble. He also began writing and performing his political songs.

He soon realized that life in East Germany was far from the communist paradise he had imagined and he wrote about this openly in his songs. "The party bosses were torn," Biermann recalls. "They were delighted by this young poet who could play the guitar so beautifully and sing such cheeky songs. They thought they just needed to bring me into line. Even today, I'm amazed that I wound up cast in the role of the heroic dragon slayer."

blocks.caption: After 11 years, Biermann was thrilled to perform in front of a large audience in West Germany again in 1976Image: Sebastian Ahlers/DHM

blocks.text: Exiled from East Germany

In 1965, East Germany's ruling Socialist Unity Party, the SED, imposed a blanket ban on Biermann performing or publishing his work. His East Berlin apartment, which was under constant surveillance, soon became a gathering place for dissidents and critical thinkers.

Yet, to his great surprise, the East German authorities allowed him to travel to Cologne, West Germany in 1976. There, around 7,000 people flocked to see him. For four and a half hours, he strummed and sang, mocking the East German regime. His songs were so popular that bootleg copies found their way back to East Germany.

On November 16, while still on tour in West Germany, Biermann heard the news on his car radio that he had been stripped of his right to continue residing in the German Democratic Republic. The regime accused him of betraying and slandering East Germany. "I felt like the ground had opened up beneath me. I was overcome with fear, everything went dark," Biermann wrote in his memoirs.

blocks.caption: Protesting together with Green Party politicians in 1983 against the impending deportation of a Turkish dissidentImage: picture-alliance/dpa/E. Steiner

blocks.text: Protest over expulsion

In a petition, leading East German intellectuals spoke out against the decision. In response, the regime stepped up surveillance of dissidents, imposed professional bans and jailed its critics. Several prominent public figures left the country.

"The SED leadership expected an angry media response from the West. What they hadn't reckoned with was that, for the very first time, a group of respected East German writers and artists would make their protest public, disguising it as a humble petition," Biermann writes.
'Always the same struggle for freedom'

Biermann sank into a deep depression. "Not just because I had been torn away from the friends I knew and loved in East Berlin, but also because I had lost my familiar mortal enemies," he says. He became involved in the peace and anti-nuclear movements and continued singing about the injustices of the world. "The world's conflicts take different forms in each generation," he says. "But it's always the same struggle for freedom."

blocks.caption: Pamela and Wolf Biermann have been a couple since 1983; she is also his managerImage: Ruff/Caro/picture alliance

blocks.text: The singer-songwriter plans to spend his 90th birthday at home in Hamburg with his wife and manager, Pamela. For the first time in his life, he says, he's skipping the birthday party, even with his 10 children. "I'm so old and I can feel my strength fading. And I know that the next day I have a major concert at the Berliner Ensemble," he told the German Press Agency (dpa).

And should he ever die, he says, he wants to be buried at Berlin's cemetery where some renowned German writers and intellectuals have been laid to rest, among them Bertolt Brecht, Anna Seghers and Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel. Quite a crowd, Biermann says. He still has a thing or two to discuss with them.
This article was originally written in German.
